chunks.traduccion: When they wished to set columns in that temple, not knowing their symmetries and seeking by what rules they might make them at once fit to bear the load and of approved beauty to the sight, they measured the print of a man's foot and referred it to the height. Finding that the foot is a sixth part of a man's height, they carried the same over to the column, and, with the thickness they gave to the base of the shaft, raised it six times that measure in height, including the capital. Thus the Doric column began to furnish in buildings the proportion, firmness, and beauty of the male body.

chunks.texto: Item postea Dianae ⟨cum cogitarent⟩ constituere aedem quaerentes novi generis speciem, isdem vestigiis ad muliebrem transtulerunt gracilitatem, et fecerunt primum columnae crassitudinem altitudinis octava parte, ut haberet speciem excelsiorem. basi spiram supposuerunt pro calceo, capitulo volutas uti capillamento concrispatos cincinnos praependentes dextra ac sinistra conlocaverunt et cymatiis et encarpis pro crinibus dispositis frontes ornaverunt truncoque toto strias uti stolarum rugas matronali more demiserunt. ita duobus discriminibus columnarum inventionem, unam virili sine ornatu nuda specie, alteram muliebri subtilitate et ornatu symmetriaque sunt mutuati.
chunks.traduccion: Afterwards, wishing to raise a temple to Diana in the aspect of a new order, they turned by the same footprints to feminine slenderness, and first made the thickness of the column an eighth part of its height, that it might have a loftier look. Beneath the base they set a base-molding (spira) in place of a shoe; on the capital they placed volutes hanging to right and left like curled ringlets of hair, and adorned the fronts with cymatia and festoons (encarpi) arranged like locks; and down the whole shaft they let flutes fall like the folds of matrons' robes. Thus by two distinct criteria they took the invention of columns: one of male aspect, bare and without ornament; the other of feminine delicacy, ornament, and symmetry.

chunks.texto: posteri vero elegantia subtilitateque iudiciorum progressi et gracilioribus modulis delectati septem crassitudinis diametros in altitudinem columnae doricae, ionicae novem constituerunt. id autem <genus>, quod Iones fecerunt primo, Ionicum est nominatum. Tertium vero, quod Corinthium dicitur, virginalis habet gracilitatis imitationem, quod virginis propter aetatis teneritatem gracilioribus membris figuratae effectus recipiunt ornatus venustiores.
chunks.traduccion: The later architects, advancing in the elegance and subtlety of their judgment and delighting in more slender modules, fixed the height of the Doric column at seven diameters of the thickness, and that of the Ionic at nine. And the order which the Ionians first made was called Ionic.

chunks.texto: eius autem capituli prima inventio sic memoratur esse facta. virgo civis Corinthia iam matura nuptiis inplicata morbo decessit. post sepulturam eius, quibus ea virgo viva pupulis delectabatur, nutrix collecta et composita in calatho pertulit ad monumentum et in summo conlocavit et, uti ea permanerent diutius subdiu, tegula texit. is calathus fortuito supra acanthi radicem fuerat conlocatus. interim pondere pressa radix acanthi media folia et cauliculos circum vernum tempus profudit, cuius cauliculi secundum calathi latera crescentes et ab angulis tegulae ponderis necessitate expressi flexuras in extremas partes volutarum facere sunt coacti.
chunks.traduccion: The first invention of this capital is recorded to have come about thus. A maiden, a citizen of Corinth, already of marriageable age, was carried off by illness. After her burial, her nurse gathered the little cups in which the girl had delighted while alive, arranged them in a basket (calathus), carried it to the tomb, and set it on top; and, that they might last longer in the open air, she covered it with a tile. The basket had by chance been placed over the root of an acanthus.

chunks.texto: tunc Callimachus, qui propter elegantiam et subtilitatem artis marmoreae ab Atheniensibus κατατηξίτεχνος () fuerat nominatus, praeteriens hoc monumentum animadvertit eum calathum et circa foliorum nascentem teneritatem, delectatusque genere et formae novitate ad id exemplar columnas apud Corinthios fecit symmetriasque constituit, et ex eo in operis perfectionibus Corinthii generis distribuit rationes.
chunks.traduccion: Meanwhile the acanthus root, pressed down by the weight, put forth about springtime leaves and little stalks through the middle; and its stalks, growing up along the sides of the basket and forced by the weight of the tile's corners, were constrained to form volutes at their ends. Then Callimachus, whom the Athenians had named katatexitechnos (κατατηξίτεχνος, 'one who refines art to the point of consuming it') for the elegance and subtlety of his work in marble, passing by this monument, noticed the basket and the tender foliage growing about it; and, delighted by the novelty of the kind and form, he made columns after that model among the Corinthians and established their symmetries, and thenceforth distributed the rules of the Corinthian order in the execution of works.

chunks.texto: eius autem capituli symmetria sic est facienda uti quanta fuerit crassitudo imae columnae, tanta sit altitudo capituli cum abaco. abaci latitudo ita habeat rationem ut quanta fuerit altitudo, tanta duo sint diagonia ab angulo ad angulum spatia. ita enim iustas habebunt frontes quoquoversus latitudines. frontes sinuentur introrsus ab extremis angulis abaci suae frontis latitudinis nona. imum capituli tantam habeat crassitudinem, quantam habet summa columna praeter apothesim et astragalum. abaci crassitudo septima capituli altitudinis.
chunks.traduccion: The symmetry of this capital is to be made so that its height, including the abacus, equals the thickness of the lower part of the column. Let the width of the abacus be in such proportion that its two diagonals, from angle to angle, are twice the height; for thus the fronts will have, on every side, the just width. Let the fronts be curved inward, from the outer angles of the abacus, by a ninth part of the width of their front. At its lower part let the capital have as much thickness as the upper part of the column, apart from the apothesis and the astragal. The thickness of the abacus is a seventh part of the capital's height.

chunks.texto: dempta abaci crassitudine, dividatur reliqua pars in partes tres, e quibus una imo folio detur. secundum folium mediam altitudinem teneat. coliculi eandem habeant altitudinem, e quibus folia nascuntur proiecta uti excipiant quae ex coliculis natae procurrunt ad extremos angulos volutae, minoresque helices infra sinum medium qui est in abaco ⟨sub⟩ flores subiecti scalpantur. flores in quattuor partibus quanta erit abaci crassitudo tam magni formentur. ita his symmetriis corinthia capitula suas habebunt exactiones. Sunt autem quae isdem columnis inponuntur capitulorum genera variis vocabulis nominata, quorum nec proprietates symmetriarum nec columnarum genus aliud nominare possumus, sed ipsorum vocabula traducta et commutata ex corinthiis et pulvinatis et doricis videmus, quorum symmetriae sunt in novarum scalpturarum translatae subtilitatem.
chunks.traduccion: The thickness of the abacus being subtracted, let the remaining part be divided into three parts, of which one is given to the lower leaf; let the second leaf occupy the middle height; let the stalks (cauliculi) have the same height, from which the projecting leaves spring that receive the volutes which, born of the stalks, run out to the extreme angles, while the smaller helices are carved within their middle—that which is on the abacus—beneath the flower. Let the flowers, on the four sides, be made as large as the thickness of the abacus. Thus, by these symmetries, the Corinthian capitals will have their due proportions.

chunks.texto: Quoniam autem de generibus columnarum origines et inventiones supra sunt scriptae, non alienum mihi videtur isdem rationibus de ornamentis eorum quemadmodum sunt prognata et quibus principiis et originibus inventa dicere. in aedificiis omnibus insuper conlocatur materiatio variis vocabulis nominata. ea autem uti in nominationibus, ita in re varias habet utilitates. trabes enim supra columnas et parastaticas et antas ponuntur, in contignationibus tigna et axes. sub tectis, si maiora spatia sunt, et transtra et capreoli, si commoda, columen et cantherii prominentes ad extremam suggrundationem. supra cantherios templa, deinde insuper sub tegulas asseres ita prominentes uti parietes proiecturis eorum tegantur.
chunks.traduccion: But since the origins and inventions of the kinds of columns have been set out above, it does not seem out of place to treat in the same way of their ornaments: how they arose and from what principles and origins they derive. In every building there is set, above, a framework of timber called by various names; and this framework, just as it varies in its names, so too it varies in its uses. For the beams (trabes) rest upon the columns, the pilasters (parastaticae) and the antae; in the floor-framing are placed the joists (tigna) and boards; under the roofs, where the spans are larger, the cross-beams (transtra) and the braces (capreoli); where they are moderate, the ridge-beam (columen) and the rafters (cantherii) that project to the edge of the eaves (suggrundatio); over the rafters, the purlins (templa); and then, above, beneath the tiles, the laths (asseres) projecting so that the walls are covered by their overhang.

chunks.texto: ita unaquaeque res et locum et genus et ordinem proprium tuetur. e quibus rebus et a materiatura fabrili in lapideis et marmoreis aedium sacrarum aedificationibus artifices dispositiones eorum scalpturis sunt imitati et eas inventiones persequendas putaverunt. ideo quod antiqui fabri quodam in loco aedificantes, cum ita ab interioribus parietibus ad extremas partes tigna prominentia habuissent conlocata, inter tigna struxerunt supraque coronas et fastigia venustiore specie fabrilibus operibus ornaverunt, tum proiecturas tignorum quantum eminebant ad lineam et perpendiculum parietum praesecuerunt, quae species cum invenusta îs visa esset tabellas ita formatas uti nunc fiunt triglyphi contra tignorum praecisiones in fronte fixerunt et eas cera caerulea depinxerunt ut praecisiones tignorum tectae non offenderent visum. ita divisiones triglyphorum et ⟨met⟩oparum tignorum dispositione et intertigniûm habere in doricis operibus coeperunt.
chunks.traduccion: Thus each thing keeps its own place, kind, and order. Hence, taking their model from timber carpentry, the craftsmen imitated in their carvings—in the stone and marble construction of temples—the arrangement of those members, and judged that such discoveries should be followed. For the ancient carpenters, building in a certain place, once they had set the beams (tigna) projecting from the inner walls out to the outermost parts, raised their structure between the beams and, above, adorned the cornices and pediments with carpentry of more graceful aspect; then they cut back the projections of the beams, as far as they jutted out, to the line and the vertical of the walls. And since that aspect seemed to them ungraceful, they fixed on the front, against the cut ends of the beams, small tablets shaped as triglyphs are now made, and painted them with blue wax, so that the cut ends of the beams, thus covered, should not offend the eye. So, imitating the divisions of the beams, they began to have in Doric works the arrangement of triglyphs and, between beam and beam, the metopes.

chunks.texto: postea alii in aliis operibus ad perpendiculum triglyphorum cantherios prominentes proiecerunt eorumque proiecturas simaverunt. ex eo uti tignorum dispositionibus triglyphi, ita e cantheriorum proiecturis mutulorum sub coronis ratio est inventa. ita fere in operibus lapideis et marmoreis mutuli inclinatis scalpturis deformantur, quod imitatio est cantheriorum. etenim necessario propter stillicidia proclinati conlocantur. ergo et triglyphorum et mutulorum in doricis operibus ratio ex ea imitatione inventa est.
chunks.traduccion: Afterwards others, in other works, carried the projecting rafters out to the vertical of the triglyphs and gave their projections a cyma (sima) profile. Hence, just as the triglyphs arose from the arrangement of the joists, so from the projections of the rafters the principle of the mutules (mutuli) beneath the cornices was found. Thus, generally, in works of stone and marble the mutules are carved with an inward slope, since they are an imitation of the rafters; for these are necessarily set sloping on account of the rain-drip (stillicidia). Therefore the principle of both the triglyphs and the mutules in Doric works was discovered from that imitation.

chunks.texto: Non enim quemadmodum nonnulli errantes dixerunt fenestrarum imagines esse triglyphos ita potest esse, quod in angulis contraque tetrantes columnarum triglyphi constituuntur, quibus in locis omnino non patitur res fenestras fieri. dissolvuntur enim angulorum in aedificiis iuncturae, si in îs fenestrarum fuerint lumina relicta. etiamque ubi nunc triglyphi constituuntur si ibi luminum spatia fuisse iudicabuntur, isdem rationibus denticuli in ionicis fenestrarum occupavisse loca videbuntur. utraque enim et inter denticulos et inter triglyphos quae sunt intervalla metopae nominantur. ὀπαι enim Graeci tignorum cubicula et asserum appellant, uti nostri ea cava columbaria. ita quod inter duas opas est intertignium, id μετόπη est apud eos nominata Ita.
chunks.traduccion: For it cannot be, as some have said in error, that triglyphs are images of windows; because triglyphs are set at the corners and opposite the quarter-points (tetrantes) of the columns—places where it is by no means possible to make windows. For the joints at the corners of buildings would be broken apart if window-openings were left in them. And further, if it were judged that, where triglyphs now stand, there had once been openings for light, then by the same reasoning the dentils in the Ionic would be supposed to have occupied the place of windows. For in both cases the intervals—both those between the dentils and those between the triglyphs—are called metopes. For the Greeks call the sockets (cubilia) of the beams and of the laths ὀπαί, just as ours call those hollows columbaria. Thus what lies between two ὀπαί, the inter-beam space, they name μετόπη.

chunks.texto: Uti autem in doricis triglyphorum et mutulorum est inventa ratio, item in ionicis denticulorum constitutio propriam in operibus habet rationem, et quemadmodum mutuli cantheriorum proiecturae ferunt imaginem, sic in ionicis denticuli ex proiecturis asserum habent imitationem. itaque in graecis operibus nemo sub mutulo denticulos constituit. non enim possunt subtus cantherios asseres esse. quod ergo supra cantherios et templa in veritate debet esse conlocatum, id in imaginibus si infra constitutum fuerit mendosam habebit operis rationem. etiam quod antiqui non probaverunt neque instituerunt in fastigiis <mutulos aut> denticulos fieri sed puras coronas, ideo quod nec cantherii nec asseres contra fastigiorum frontes distribuuntur nec possunt prominere, sed ad stillicidia proclinati conlocantur. ita quod non potest in veritate fieri, id non putaverunt in imaginibus factum posse certam rationem habere.
chunks.traduccion: And just as in the Doric the principle of triglyphs and mutules was found, so in the Ionic the disposition of the dentils has its own basis in the works; and just as the mutules reproduce the image of the projections of the rafters, so in the Ionic the dentils imitate the projections of the laths (asseres). For this reason, in Greek works no one sets dentils beneath mutules, since laths cannot lie beneath rafters. So what in reality must be set above the rafters and the purlin, if in the images it is placed below, will give the work a faulty design. The ancients, moreover, did not approve or establish the making of ⟨mutules or⟩ dentils on the pediments, but only plain cornices, because neither the rafters nor the laths are distributed against the fronts of the pediments, nor can they project, but are set sloping towards the drip. Thus, what cannot be done in reality, they judged could have no sound design when done in the images.

chunks.texto: omnia enim certa proprietate et a veris naturae deducta moribus transduxerunt in operum perfectiones, et ea probaverunt quorum explicationes in disputationibus rationem possunt habere veritatis. itaque ex eis originibus symmetrias et proportiones uniuscuiusque generis constitutas reliquerunt. quorum ingressus persecutus de ionicis et corinthiis institutionibus supra dixi, nunc vero doricam rationem summamque eius speciem breviter exponam.
chunks.traduccion: For they carried over all things into the perfection of their works with sure propriety and drawn from the true laws of nature, and they approved only those things whose explanations can uphold, in debate, the principle of truth. And so, from those origins, they left the symmetries and proportions of each kind established. Having traced their development, I have spoken above of the Ionic and Corinthian rules; now, however, I shall briefly set out the Doric system and the general character of its appearance.

chunks.texto: Nonnulli antiqui architecti negaverunt dorico genere aedes sacras oportere fieri, quod mendosae et disconvenientes in his symmetriae conficiebantur. itaque negavit Arcesius, item Pytheos, non minus Hermogenes. nam is cum paratam habuisset marmoris copiam in doricae aedis perfectionem, <> commutavit ex eadem copia et eam ionicam Libero Patri fecit. sed tamen non quod invenusta est species aut genus aut formae dignitas, sed quod inpedita est distributio et incommoda in opere triglyphorum et lacunariorum [distributione].
chunks.traduccion: Some ancient architects denied that sacred buildings should be built in the Doric style, because they created false and inappropriate symmetries. And so Arcesius denied it, Pythius as well, and Hermogenes no less. For when he had prepared a supply of marble for the completion of the Doric building, he changed it from the same supply and made it Ionic for the Free Father. However, it is not that the species or genus or dignity of the form are unattractive, but rather that the distribution is complicated and inconvenient in the arrangement of the triglyphs and ceiling work.

chunks.texto: namque necesse est triglyphos constitui contra medios tetrantes columnarum, metopasque quae inter triglyphos fient aeque longas esse quam altas. contraque in angulares columnas triglyphi in extremis partibus constituuntur et non contra medios tetrantes. ita metopae, quae proximae ad angulares triglyphos fiunt, non exeunt quadratae sed oblongiores triglyphi dimidia latitudine. at qui metopas aequales volunt facere, intercolumnia extrema contrahunt triglyphi dimidia latitudine. hoc autem sive metoparum longitudinibus sive intercolumniorum contractionibus efficietur, est mendosum. quapropter antiqui vitare visi sunt in aedibus sacris doricae symmetriae rationem.
chunks.traduccion: For the triglyphs must be set opposite the middle quarter-points (tetrantes) of the columns, and the metopes between the triglyphs must be as long as they are high. But at the corner columns the triglyphs are placed at the ends, not opposite the middle points; and so the metopes nearest the corner triglyphs come out not square but oblong, broader by half the width of a triglyph. Those who wish to make the metopes equal contract the outermost intercolumniations by half the width of a triglyph. But this—whether done by lengthening the metopes or by narrowing the intercolumniations—is faulty. For this reason the ancients seem to have avoided the scheme of Doric symmetry in their temples.

chunks.texto: Nos autem exponimus, uti ordo postulat, quemadmodum a praeceptoribus accepimus, uti si qui voluerit his rationibus attendens ita ingredi, habeat proportiones explicatas, quibus emendatas et sine vitiis efficere possit aedium sacrarum dorico more perfectiones. frons aedis doricae in loco quo columnae constituuntur dividatur, si tetrastylos erit, in partes XXVII, si hexastylos, XXXXII. ex his pars una erit modulus, qui graece ἐμβάτης dicitur, cuius moduli constitutione ratiocinationibus efficiuntur omnis operis distributiones.
chunks.traduccion: We, however, set it forth as the order of treatment requires, just as we received it from our teachers, so that anyone who wishes to proceed with attention to these rules may have the proportions laid out by which he can achieve, corrected and free of faults, the perfection of sacred buildings in the Doric manner. The front of a Doric temple, at the place where the columns are set, is divided—if it is tetrastyle—into twenty-seven parts; if hexastyle, into forty-two. One of these parts will be the module, which in Greek is called ἐμβάτης (embátes), by whose establishment all the distributions of the work are determined by calculation.

chunks.texto: Crassitudo columnarum erit duorum modulorum, altitudo cum capitulo XIIII. capituli crassitudo unius moduli, latitudo duorum et moduli sextae partis. crassitudo capituli dividatur in partes tres, e quibus una plinthus cum cymatio fiat, altera echinus cum anulis, tertia hypotrachelion. contrahatur columna ita uti in tertio libro de ionicis est scriptum. epistylii altitudo unius moduli cum taenia et guttis, taenia moduli septima, guttarum longitudo sub taenia contra triglyphos alta cum regula parte sexta moduli praependeat. item epistylii latitudo ima respondeat hypotrachelio summae columnae. supra epistylium conlocandi sunt triglyphi cum suis metopis, alti unius et dimidiati moduli, lati in fronte unius moduli, ita divisi ut in angularibus columnis et in mediis contra tetrantes medios sint conlocati, et intercolumniis reliquis bini, in mediis pronao et postico terni. ita relaxatis mediis intervallis, sine inpeditionibus aditus accedentibus erit ad deorum simulacra.
chunks.traduccion: The thickness of the columns will be two modules, and their height, including the capital, fourteen. The thickness of the capital is one module, and its width two and one-sixth modules. The thickness of the capital is divided into three parts: one forms the plinth with the cymatium; the second, the echinus with its annulets; the third, the hypotrachelion. The column is diminished as is written, for the Ionic, in the third book. The height of the architrave (epistylium) is one module, with the taenia and the guttae; the taenia a seventh of the module; the length of the guttae, beneath the taenia and in line with the triglyphs, hangs down to the line of the taenia, and their width is a sixth of the module. Likewise the lower face of the architrave should answer to the hypotrachelion at the top of the column. Above the architrave the triglyphs are set with their metopes, one and a half modules high and one module wide at the front, so arranged that at the corner columns and the middle ones they stand opposite the middle quarter-points (tetrantes), with two in the remaining intercolumniations and three in the middle of the pronaos and the rear portico. Thus, with the central intervals left open, there will be unimpeded access for those approaching the images of the gods.

chunks.texto: triglyphorum latitudo dividatur in partes sex, ex quibus partibus quinque in medio, duae dimidiae dextra ac sinistra designentur regula. una in medio deformetur femur, quod graece μηρός dicitur. secundum eam canaliculi ad normae cacumen inprimantur. ex ordine eorum dextra ac sinistra altera femina constituantur. in extremis partibus semicanaliculi intervertantur. triglyphis ita conlocatis, metopae quae sunt inter triglyphos aeque altae sint quam longae, item in extremis angulis hemimetopia sint inpressa dimidia moduli latitudine. ita enim erit ut omnia vitia et metoparum et intercolumniorum et lacunariorum, quod aequales divisiones factae erunt, emendentur.
chunks.traduccion: The width of the triglyphs is divided into six parts, of which five are marked out in the middle, and two halves, right and left, by the rule. In the middle one thigh (femur) is shaped, which in Greek is called μηρός; along it the channels are cut to the point of the set-square (norma); on either side of them, right and left, the other thighs (femina) are formed; at the outer edges the half-channels are turned in. With the triglyphs thus placed, the metopes between the triglyphs should be as high as they are long; likewise at the outermost corners half-metopes are impressed, half a module wide. For thus it will come about that all the faults—of the metopes, of the intercolumniations, and of the coffers—are corrected, since the divisions will have been made equal.

chunks.texto: triglyphi capitula sexta parte moduli sunt faciunda. supra triglyphorum capitula corona est conlocanda in proiectura dimidiae et sextae partis habens cymatium doricum in imo, alterum in summo. item cum cymatiis corona crassa ex dimidia moduli. dividendae autem sunt in corona ima ad perpendiculum triglyphorum et medias metopas viarum directiones et guttarum distributiones, ita uti guttae sex in longitudinem, tres in latitudinem pateant. reliqua spatia, quod latiores sunt metopae quam triglyphi, pura relinquantur aut flumina scalpantur, ad ipsumque mentum coronae incidatur linea quae scotia dicitur. reliqua omnia, tympana simae coronae, quemadmodum supra scriptum est in ionicis, ita perficiantur.
chunks.traduccion: The capitals of the triglyphs are made one-sixth of a module. Above the triglyph capitals a cornice (corona) is to be set, with a projection of one-half and one-sixth, having a Doric cymatium below and another above. With the cornice, then, and the cymatia, the whole cornice is to be made half a module thick. On the front of the cornice, above the triglyphs and the metopes, are distributed—plumb with the triglyphs and the centers of the metopes—the channels (viae) and the arrangement of the guttae, so that six guttae appear lengthwise and three across. The remaining spaces, since the metopes are wider than the triglyphs, are left plain or carved with small figures of gods. And on the very underside (mentum) of the cornice a line is cut which in Greek is called σκωτία (scotia). Everything else—the capitals of the columns, the architraves, the cornices—is finished as written above for the Ionic.

chunks.texto: Haec ratio in operibus diastylis erit constituta. si vero systylon et monotriglyphon opus erit faciundum, frons aedis, si tetrastylos erit, dividatur in partes XVIIII S, si hexastylos erit, dividatur in partes XXVIIII S. ex his pars una erit modulus, ad quem uti supra scriptum est dividantur.
chunks.traduccion: This scheme will be established for diastyle works. But if a systyle and monotriglyph work is to be made, the front of the temple, if tetrastyle, is divided into nineteen and a half parts; if hexastyle, into twenty-nine and a half. Of these, one part will be the module, by which everything is divided as written above.

chunks.texto: ita supra singula epistylia et metopae et triglyphi bini erunt conlocandi, in angularibus hoc amplius dimidiatus et quantum est spatium hemitriglyphi id accedit. in mediano contra fastigium trium triglyphorum et trium metoparum spatium distabit, quo latius medium intercolumnium accedentibus ad aedem habeat laxamentum et adversus simulacra deorum aspectus dignitatem.
chunks.traduccion: Thus, above each architrave side, metopes and triglyphs will be placed in pairs; at the corners, this goes further, so much so that the space of the hemiglyph is reduced by half. In the middle, against the pediment, there will be a space of three triglyphs and three metopes, so that the wider middle of the intercolumniations will have a relief for those approaching the house and a dignity of appearance in front of the images of the gods.

chunks.texto: Columnas autem striari XX striis oportet. quae si planae erunt, angulos habeant XX designatos. sin autem excavabuntur, sic est forma facienda ita uti quam magnum est intervallum striae, tam magnis striaturae paribus lateribus quadratum describatur, in medio autem quadrato circini centrum conlocetur et agatur linea rotundationis, quae quadrationis angulos tangat, et quantum erit curvaturae inter rotundationem et quadratam descriptionem, tantum ad formam excaventur. ita dorica columna sui generis striaturae habebit perfectionem.
chunks.traduccion: But the columns must be fluted with 20 flutes. If they are flat, let them have 20 designated angles. But if they are to be excavated, the form will be made so that the greater the interval of the fluting, the greater the equal sides of the fluting will be, describing the square; and in the middle of the square of the circle the center is placed, and a rounding line is drawn, which touches the angles of the square, and the extension of the curvature between the rounding and the description of the square should only be excavated for the form. Thus the Doric column will have the perfection of its type of fluting.

chunks.texto: de adiectione eius qua media adaugetur, uti in tertio volumine de ionicis est perscripta, ita et in his transferatur. Quoniam exterior species symmetriarum et corinthiorum et doricorum et ionicorum est perscripta, necesse est etiam interiores cellarum pronaique distributiones explicare.
chunks.traduccion: As for the addition to it, whereby half is added, as is recorded in the third volume on Ionic matters, so too it is carried over in these.

chunks.texto: distribuitur autem longitudo aedis uti latitudo sit longitudinis dimidiae partis, ipsaque cella parte quarta longior sit, quam est latitudo, cum pariete, qui paries valvarum habuerit conlocationem. reliquae tres partes pronai ad antas parietum procurrant, quae antae columnarum crassitudinem habere debent. et si aedes erit latitudine maior quam pedes XX, duae columnae inter duas antas interponantur, quae disiungant pteromatos et pronai spatium. item intercolumnia tria, quae erunt inter antas et columnas, pluteis marmoreis sive ex intestino opere factis intercludantur ita uti fores habeant, per quas itinera pronao fiant.
chunks.traduccion: The length of the temple is distributed so that the width is half the length, and the cella itself is one quarter longer than it is wide, including the wall in which the doors are set. The remaining three parts run forward, for the pronaos, to the antae of the walls; these antae should have the thickness of the columns. And if the temple is more than twenty feet wide, let two columns be set between the two antae, separating the space of the surrounding colonnade (pteroma) from that of the pronaos. Likewise, let the three intercolumniations between the antae and the columns be closed with marble screens or panels of joinery, leaving doors in them by which one may enter the pronaos.

chunks.texto: item si maior erit latitudo quam pedes XL, columnae contra regiones columnarum, quae inter antas sunt, introrsus conlocentur. et hae altitudinem habeant aeque quam quae sunt in fronte, crassitudines autem earum extenuentur his rationibus uti si octava parte erunt quae sunt in fronte, hae fiant X parte, sin autem VIIII aut decima, pro rata parte. in concluso enim aere si quae extenuatae erunt, non discernentur. sin autem videbuntur graciliores, cum exterioribus fuerint striae <XX aut> XXIIII, in his faciendae erunt XXVIII aut XXXII. ita quod detrahitur de corpore scapi, striarum numero adiecto adaugebitur ratione quo minus videatur, et ita exaequabitur dispari ratione columnarum crassitudo.
chunks.traduccion: If the temple is more than forty feet wide, place interior columns opposite those standing between the antae. Their height should equal that of the front columns, but their diameters should be reduced: where the front columns have a diameter one-eighth of their height, the interior ones should have one-tenth; where the front proportion is one-ninth or one-tenth, reduce the interior diameters proportionately. In an enclosed space the reduction will be less apparent. If they nevertheless seem too slender, give the interior columns twenty-eight or thirty-two flutes where the exterior columns have ⟨twenty or⟩ twenty-four. The greater number of flutes compensates visually for the reduction in the shaft, allowing columns of unequal diameters to appear equivalent.

chunks.texto: hoc autem efficit ea ratio quod oculus plura et crebriora signa tangendo maiore visus circumitione pervagatur. namque si duae columnae aeque crassae lineis circummetientur, e quibus una sit non striata altera striata, et circa striglium cava et angulos striarum linea corpora tangat, tametsi columnae aeque crassae fuerint, lineae quae circumdatae erunt <non erunt> aequales, quod striarum et striglium circuitus maiorem efficit lineae longitudinem. sin autem hoc ita videbitur, non est alienum in angustis locis et in concluso spatio graciliores columnarum symmetrias in opere constituere, cum habeamus adiutricem striarum temperaturam.
chunks.traduccion: This comes about because the eye, touching more numerous and frequent marks, ranges over a wider compass of vision. For if two equally thick columns are measured round with lines, one unfluted and the other fluted, and the line follows the bodies along the hollows of the flutes and the edges (striglium) between them, then, even though the columns are equally thick, the lines drawn around them will not be equal, because the circuit of the flutes and their channels gives the line a greater length. And if this is so, it is not out of place, in narrow places and enclosed spaces, to employ more slender proportions in the columns, since we have the tempering of the fluting to help us.

chunks.texto: ipsius autem cellae parietum crassitudinem pro rata parte magnitudinis fieri oportet, dum antae eorum crassitudinibus columnarum sint aequales. et si ex structis futuri sunt, quam minutissimis caementis struantur, sin autem quadrato saxo aut marmore, maxime modicis paribusque videtur esse faciundum, quod media coagmenta medii lapides continentes firmiorem facient omnis operis perfectionem, item circum coagmenta et cubilia eminentes expressiones graphicoteran efficient in aspectu delectationem.
chunks.traduccion: The thickness of the walls of the cella itself should be made in proportion to its size, provided that its antae are equal to the thickness of the columns. And if they are to be of rubble-work, let them be built with the smallest possible aggregate; but if of squared stone or marble, it is best to use modest and equal pieces, since the middle stones, binding the central joints, will make the whole work firmer in its finish; and moreover the projecting reliefs around the joints and the beds will produce a more elegant delight to the eye.

chunks.texto: Regiones autem, quas debent spectare aedes sacrae deorum inmortalium, sic erunt constituendae, uti, si nulla ratio inpedierit liberaque fuerit potestas, aedis signumque, quod erit in cella conlocatum, spectet ad vespertinam caeli regionem, uti, qui adierint ad aram immolantes aut sacrificia facientes, spectent ad partem caeli orientis et simulacrum, quod erit in aede, et ita vota suscipientes contueantur aedem et orientem caelum ipsaque simulacra videantur exaudientia contueri supplicantes et sacrificantes, quod aras omnes deorum necesse esse videatur ad orientem spectare.
chunks.traduccion: The directions faced by the temples of the immortal gods should be established as follows. If nothing prevents it and the choice is free, let the temple and the image within its cella face the western part of the sky, so that those approaching the altar to sacrifice look towards the east and the image in the temple. In taking their vows they will thus behold both the temple and the rising sky, while the images appear to listen to those praying and sacrificing. For the altars of all the gods should, it seems, face east.

chunks.texto: sin autem loci natura interpellaverit, tunc convertendae sunt earum regionum constitutiones, uti quam plurima pars moenium e templis earum conspiciatur. item si secundum flumina aedis sacra fiet, ita uti Aegypto circa Nilum, ad fluminis ripas videntur spectare debere. similiter si circum vias publicas erunt aedificia deorum, ita constituantur uti praetereuntes possint respicere et in conspectu salutationes facere.
chunks.traduccion: But if the nature of the site interferes, then the orientation of those regions must be changed, so that as much of the city as possible may be seen from the temples of the gods. Likewise, if sacred temples are built beside rivers—as in Egypt, around the Nile—they ought to face the river’s banks. And similarly, if the buildings of the gods stand along the public roads, let them be so arranged that passers-by may see them from the front and make their salutations in full view.

chunks.texto: Ostiorum autem et eorum antepagmentorum in aedibus hae sunt rationes, uti primum constituatur, quot genera sint [futurae]. Genera sunt enim thyromaton haec: doricum, ionicum, atticurges. Horum ⟨dorici generis⟩ symmetriae conspiciuntur his rationibus, uti corona summa, quae supra antepagmentum superius inponitur, aeque librata sit capitulis summis columnarum, quae in pronao fuerint. Lumen autem thyretri constituatur sic, uti quae altitudo aedis a pavimento ad lacunaria fuerit, dividatur in partes tres semis et ex eis duae partes ⟨semis⟩ lumini valvarum altitudine constituantur. Haec autem dividatur in partes XII et ex eis quinque et dimidia latitudo luminis fiat in imo. Et in summo contrahatur, si erit lumen ab imo ad sedecim pedes, antepagmenti III parte; ⟨si⟩ XVI pedum ad XXV, superior pars luminis contrahatur antepagmenti parte IIII; si ab pedibus XXV ad XXX, summa pars contrahatur antepagmenti parte VIII. Reliqua, quo altiora erunt, ad perpendiculum videntur oportere conlocari.
chunks.traduccion: The rules for temple doors and their frames are as follows. First, the different kinds must be distinguished: Doric, Ionic and Attic. The Doric proportions follow these principles. The upper cornice above the lintel should be level with the tops of the column capitals in the pronaos. Establish the clear opening by dividing the height of the temple, from pavement to coffering, into three and a half parts, and assigning two and a half to the height of the doorway. Divide this height into twelve parts and make the lower width of the opening five and a half of them. If the opening is no more than sixteen feet high, contract it at the top by one-third of the jamb; from sixteen to twenty-five feet, by one-quarter; and from twenty-five to thirty feet, by one-eighth. Taller openings should, it seems, have vertical sides.

chunks.texto: ipsa autem antepagmenta contrahantur in summo suae crassitudinis XIIII parte. supercilii crassitudo quanta antepagmentorum in summa parte erit crassitudo. cymatium faciundum est antepagmenti parte sexta, proiectura autem quanta est eius crassitudo. sculpendum est cymatium lesbium cum astragalo. supra cymatium quod erit in supercilio, conlocandum est hyperthyrum crassitudine supercilii, et in eo scalpendum est cymatium doricum, astragalum lesbium. sima scalptura corona plana cum cymatio, proiectura autem eius erit quanta altitudo. supercilii quod supra antepagmenta inponitur, dextra atque sinistra proiecturae sic sunt faciundae uti crepidines excurrant et in unguem ipso cymatio coniungantur.
chunks.traduccion: Let the jambs themselves be drawn in at the top by a fourteenth part of their thickness. Let the thickness of the lintel (supercilium) equal that of the jambs at their upper part. The cyma is made a sixth part of the jamb, and its projection equal to its thickness; a Lesbian cyma with an astragal is to be carved. Above the cyma that crowns the lintel is placed the hyperthyrum, of the thickness of the lintel, and on it a Doric cyma and a Lesbian astragal are carved. At the very top a plain cornice with its cyma is carved, its projection equal to its height. Of the lintel that rests upon the jambs, the projections to right and left are so made that the fillets run out and join in a mitre with the cyma itself.

chunks.texto: Sin autem ionico genere futura erunt, lumen altum ad eundem modum quemadmodum in doricis fieri videtur. latitudo constituatur ut altitudo dividatur in partes duas et dimidiam, eiusque partis unius ima luminis fiat latitudo. contracturae ita uti in doricis. crassitudo antepagmentorum ⟨ex⟩ altitudine luminis in fronte XIIII parte, cymatium huius crassitudinis sexta. reliqua pars praeter cymatium dividatur in partes XII. harum trium prima corsa fiat cum astragalo, secunda quattuor, tertia quinque, et eae aeque corsae cum astragalis circumcurrant.
chunks.traduccion: For Ionic doors, the height of the clear opening should be determined as for Doric doors. Establish the width by dividing the height into two and a half parts and making the lower width one of them. The contractions follow the Doric rules. The face of the frame should be one-fourteenth of the opening’s height, and its cyma one-sixth of that thickness. Divide the remainder, excluding the cyma, into twelve parts: assign three to the first fascia with its astragal, four to the second and five to the third. These fasciae and their astragals should continue around the opening.

chunks.texto: Hyperthyra autem ad eundem modum componantur quemadmodum in doricis. Pro crepidinibus ancones, sive parotides vocantur, excalptae dextra ac sinistra praependeant ad imi supercilii libramentum, praeter folium. Eae habeant in fronte crassitudinem ex antepagmenti tribus partibus, imo quarta parte graciliore quam superiora. Fores ita compingantur, uti scapi cardinales sint ex latitudine luminis totius XII parte. Inter duos scapos tympana ex XII partibus habeant ternas partes.
chunks.traduccion: The hyperthyra are composed in the same way as in the Doric, in proportional parts. The consoles (ancones)—or parotides, as they are also called—carved to right and left, hang down to the level of the lower lintel, save for the acanthus leaf. Let them have, at the front, a thickness of two of the three parts of the jamb, and at the bottom be a fourth part more slender than above. Let the leaves (fores) be framed so that the hinge-stiles (scapi cardinales) are a twelfth part of the whole width of the opening. Between the two stiles let the panels (tympana) have three of the twelve parts.

chunks.texto: inpagibus distributiones ita fient uti divisis altitudinibus in partes V duae superiori, tres inferiori designentur. super medium medii inpages conlocentur, ex reliquis alii in summo alii in imo compingantur. altitudo inpagis fiat tympani tertia parte, cymatium sexta parte inpagis. scaporum latitudines inpagis dimidia parte, item replum de inpage dimidia et sexta parte. scapi qui sunt secundum antepagmentum, dimidium inpagis constituantur. sin autem valvatae erunt, altitudines ita manebunt, in latitudinem adiciatur amplius foris latitudo. si quadriforis futura est, altitudo adiciatur.
chunks.traduccion: The rails (impages) are distributed by dividing the height into five parts: two are assigned to the upper, three to the lower. Over the middle let the middle rails be set; of the rest, some are framed at the top, others at the bottom. Let the height of the rail be a third part of the panel, and its cyma a sixth of the rail. Let the width of the stiles be half the rail; the meeting-stile (replum), half plus a sixth of the rail. The stiles next to the jambs are made half the rail. But if the doors are to be folding (valvatae), the heights remain the same, and to the width is added that of another leaf; if it is to be four-leaved, height is added.

chunks.texto: Atticurge autem isdem rationibus perficiuntur quibus dorica. praeterea corsae sub cymatiis in antepagmentis circumdantur, quae ita distribui debent uti antepagmenti praeter cymatium ex partibus VII habeant duas partes. ipsaque non fiunt clathrata neque bifora sed valvata, et aperturas habent in exteriores partes. Quas rationes aedium sacrarum in formationibus oporteat fieri <doricis> ionicis corinthiisque operibus, quoad potui attingere, veluti legitimis moribus exposui. nunc de tuscanicis dispositionibus quemadmodum institui oporteat dicam.
chunks.traduccion: Attic doors are executed by the same rules as the Doric. Moreover, beneath the cymas, bands (corsae) are set round the jambs, which are to be so distributed that, of the seven parts of the jamb—apart from the cyma—they occupy two parts. And these doors are made neither latticed nor folding, but with leaves (valvatae), and they open outward. I have set forth, as far as I have been able, according to established usage, what rules should be followed in designing sacred temples in Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian works. Now I shall speak of how the Tuscan arrangements ought to be set out.

chunks.texto: locus, in quo aedis constituetur, cum habuerit in longitudine sex partes, una dempta reliquum quod erit latitudini detur. longitudo autem dividatur bipertito et quae pars erit interior, cellarum spatiis designetur, quae erit proxima fronti, columnarum dispositioni relinquatur.
chunks.traduccion: The place where the temple is to be raised, when it has six parts in length, one part being taken away, let the remainder be given to the breadth. Let the length be divided into two parts: the inner part be assigned to the spaces of the cellae, and that nearest the front reserved for the arrangement of the columns.

chunks.texto: item latitudo dividatur in partes X. ex his ternae partes dextra ac sinistra cellis minoribus sive ibi alae futurae sunt dentur, reliquae quattuor mediae aedi attribuantur. spatium quod erit ante cellas in pronao, ita columnis designetur ut angulares contra antas, parietum extremorum e regione, conlocentur, duae mediae e regione parietum qui inter antas et mediam aedem fuerint, ita distribuantur, et inter antas et columnas priores per medium isdem regionibus alterae disponantur. eaeque sint ima crassitudine altitudinis parte VII, altitudo tertia parte latitudinis templi, summaque columna quarta parte crassitudinis imae contrahatur.
chunks.traduccion: Likewise, let the breadth be divided into ten parts. Of these, three on the right and three on the left be given to the lesser cellae—or to the wings, if there be any; the remaining four, in the middle, be assigned to the temple. The space before the cellae, in the pronaos, be marked out with columns so that the corner ones stand opposite the antae, in the line of the outermost walls; the two central ones in the line of the walls that lie between the antae and the middle of the temple; and between the antae and the front columns, through the middle, let others be set in those same lines. Let these be, at the bottom, of a thickness equal to a seventh part of their height; the height a third part of the breadth of the temple; and let the top of the column be drawn in by a fourth part of the lower thickness.

chunks.texto: Spirae earum altae dimidia parte crassitudinis fiant. habeant spirae earum plinthum ad circinum, altam suae crassitudinis dimidia parte, torum insuper cum apophysi crassum quantum plinthus. capituli altitudo dimidia crassitudinis. abaci latitudo quanta ima crassitudo columnae. capitulique crassitudo dividatur in partes tres, e quibus una plintho, quae est abacus, detur, altera echino, tertia hypotrachelio cum apophysi.
chunks.traduccion: Let their bases (spirae) be half as high as their thickness. Let the bases have a circular plinth, half as high as their thickness, and above it a torus with its apophyge, as thick as the plinth. The height of the capital, half the thickness. The width of the abacus, equal to the lower thickness of the column. Let the thickness of the capital be divided into three parts: one given to the plinth, which is on the abacus; another to the echinus; and the third to the hypotrachelion with its apophyge.

chunks.texto: Supra columnas trabes compactiles inponantur ut altitudinis modulis îs, qui a magnitudine operis postulabuntur. eaeque trabes compactiles eam habeant crassitudinem, quanta summae columnae erit hypotrachelium, et ita sint compactae subscudibus et securiclis, ut compactura duorum digitorum habeant laxationem. cum enim inter se tangunt et non spiramentum et perflatum venti recipiunt, concalefaciuntur et celeriter putrescunt.
chunks.traduccion: Upon the columns let framed beams be placed, of a height in modules such as the magnitude of the work demands; and let these framed beams be so laid that they have a width equal to that of the tops of the columns, and be joined with tenons and dovetails, leaving in the joint a play of two fingers: for when they touch one another and admit no breath or draught of air, they grow hot and quickly rot.

chunks.texto: supra trabes et supra parietes traiecturae mutulorum parte IIII altitudinis columnae proiciantur, item in eorum frontibus antepagmenta figantur, supraque îs tympanum fastigii structura seu de materia conlocetur. supraque eûm fastigium, columen, cantherii, templa ita sunt conlocanda ut stillicidium tecti absoluti tertiario respondeat.
chunks.traduccion: Above the beams and above the walls, let the projections of the mutules jut out a fourth part of the height of the column; and on their fronts let the door-casings (antepagmenta) be fixed. Above this let the tympanum of the pediment be set, of masonry or of timber; and above it the ridge-beam (columen), the rafters (cantherii), and the purlins (templa), so arranged that the drip of the finished roof answers to a third.

chunks.texto: Fiunt autem aedes rotundae, e quibus aliae monopteroe sine cella columnatae constituuntur, aliae peripteroe dicuntur. quae sine cella fiunt, tribunal habent et ascensum ex sua diametro tertiae partis. insuper stylobatam columnae constituuntur tam altae quanta ab extremis parietibus est diametros stylobatarum, crassae altitudinis suae cum capitulis et spiris decumae partis. epistylium altum columnae crassitudinis dimidia parte. zophorum et reliqua quae insuper inponuntur, ita uti in III volumine de symmetriis scripsi.
chunks.traduccion: Round temples are also made, of which some, called monopteral, are built colonnaded without a cella, and others are called peripteral. Those made without a cella have a platform (tribunal) and an approach of stairs a third part of their diameter. Upon the stylobates columns are raised as tall as the interval between the outermost walls, and of a thickness equal to a tenth part of their height, including base and capital. The architrave (epistylium) is half the thickness of the column. The frieze (zophorus) and the rest that is set above, as I wrote in the third book on the symmetries.

chunks.texto: Sin autem peripteros ea aedes constituetur, duo gradus et stylobata ab imo constituantur. Deinde cellae paries conlocetur cum recessu eius a stylobata circa partem latitudinis quintam, medioque valvarum locus ad aditus relinquatur; eaque cella tantam habeat diametrum praeter parietes et circumitionem, quantam altitudinem columna. Supra stylobatam columnae circum cellam isdem symmetriis, quae ⟨supra scriptae sunt,⟩ disponantur.
chunks.traduccion: If the temple is to be peripteral, provide two steps and the stylobate from the ground up. Set the cella wall approximately one-fifth of the width back from the stylobate, leaving an opening in the middle for the entrance. Excluding the walls and the surrounding passage, the cella’s diameter should equal the height of the column. Arrange the columns around the cella on the stylobate according to the proportions already given.

chunks.texto: in medio tecti ratio ita habeatur uti quanta diametros totius operis erit futura dimidia altitudo fiat tholi praeter florem, flos autem tantam habeat magnitudinem quantam habuerit columnae capitulum, praeter pyramidem. reliqua uti supra scripta sunt, isdem proportionibus atque symmetriis facienda videntur.
chunks.traduccion: In the middle, let the plan of the roof be such that, whatever the diameter of the whole work is to be, half of it be the height of the tholos, apart from the finial (flos). Let the finial have as much size as the capital of the column, apart from the pyramid. The rest is to be made by the same symmetries and proportions as written above.

chunks.texto: Item generibus aliis constituuntur aedes ex isdem symmetriis ordinatae et alio genere dispositiones habentes, uti est Castoris in circo Flaminio, et inter duos lucos Veiovis, item augustius Nemori Dianae columnis adiectis dextra ac sinistra ad umeros pronai. hoc autem genere primo facta est, uti est Castoris in circo Athenis in arce et in Attica Sunio Palladis Minervae. earum non aliae sed eaedem sunt proportiones. cellae enim longitudinibus duplices sunt ad latitudines uti reliquae, ex îs omnia quae solent esse in frontibus, ad latera sunt translata.
chunks.traduccion: Other kinds of temple follow the same proportions but employ a different arrangement: for example, the temple of Castor in the Circus Flaminius, that of Vediovis between the two sacred groves, and, on a grander scale, Diana’s temple in the Grove, with columns added on either side of the pronaos. The temples of Pallas Minerva on the Athenian Acropolis and at Sunium in Attica belong to the type exemplified by the temple of Castor in the Circus. Their proportions remain the same. As in the other temples, the cellae are twice as long as they are wide, but the elements normally placed at the front have been transferred to the sides.

chunks.texto: nonnulli etiam de tuscanicis generibus sumentes columnarum dispositiones transferunt in corinthiorum et ionicorum operum ordinationes, et quibus in locis in pronao procurrunt antae, in isdem e regione cellae parietum columnas binas conlocantes efficiunt tuscanicorum et graecorum operum communem ratiocinationem.
chunks.traduccion: Some builders also take the column arrangements of Tuscan temples and apply them to Corinthian and Ionic compositions. Where the antae project into the pronaos, they place paired columns in line with the cella walls, producing a design that combines Tuscan and Greek principles.

chunks.texto: alii vero removentes parietes aedis et adplicantes ad intercolumnia, pteromatos spatiis sublati efficiunt amplum laxamentum cellae, reliqua autem proportionibus et symmetriis isdem conservantes aliud genus figurae nominisque videntur pseudoperipterum procreavisse. haec autem genera propter usum sacrificiorum convertuntur. non enim omnibus diis isdem rationibus aedes sunt faciundae, quod alius alia varietate sacrorum religionum habet effectus.
chunks.traduccion: Others move the temple walls outward to meet the intercolumniations. By eliminating the surrounding pteroma they obtain a spacious cella, while retaining the other proportions and symmetries. In doing so they seem to have created a type with a different form and name, the pseudoperipteral temple. These types vary according to sacrificial practice: temples should not be designed on the same principles for every deity, since the effect of each cult depends on its particular rites.

chunks.texto: Omnes aedium sacrarum ratiocinationes uti mihi traditae sunt exposui ordinesque et symmetrias earum partitionibus distinxi, et quarum dispares sunt figurae et quibus discriminibus inter se sunt disparatae quoad potui significare scriptis exposui. nunc de aris deorum inmortalium uti aptam constitutionem habeant ad sacrificiorum rationem dicam.
chunks.traduccion: I have explained all the reasoning of the sacred buildings, as they have been handed down to me, and I have distinguished their orders and symmetries by their divisions, and whose disparate figures they are, and by what distinctions they arise from one another. I explained to another, as far as I could express in writing. Now I will speak of the areas of the immortal gods, so that they may have a suitable constitution as the object of sacrifices.

chunks.texto: Arae spectent ad orientem et semper inferiores sint conlocatae quam simulacra, quae fuerint in aede, uti suspicientes divinitatem, qui supplicant, et sacrificent. Disparibus altitudinibus ad sui cuiusque dei decorem componantur. Altitudines autem earum sic sunt explicandae, uti Iovi omnibusque caelestibus quam excelsissimae constituantur, Vestae Terrae Matrique humiles conlocentur. Ita idoneae his institutionibus explicabuntur modulationibus ararum deformationes. Explicatis aedium sacrarum compositionibus in hoc libro, insequenti de communium operum reddemus distributionibus explicationes.
chunks.traduccion: Altars should face east and always stand below the cult images within the temple, so that those who pray and sacrifice look upward towards the deity. Their heights should vary according to the decor appropriate to each god. For Jupiter and all the celestial gods, make the altars as high as possible; for Vesta, Earth and the Mother, set them low. These principles yield altar forms appropriate in their proportions.

chunks.texto: Qui amplioribus voluminibus, imperator, ingenii cogitationes praeceptaque explicaverunt, maximas et egregias adiecerunt suis scriptis auctoritates. quod etiam velim nostris quoque studiis res pateretur, ut amplificationibus auctoritas et in his praeceptis augeretur, sed id non est quemadmodum putatur expeditum. non enim de architectura sic scribitur uti historia aut poemata. historiae per se tenent lectores. habent enim novarum rerum varias expectationes. poematorum vero [carminum] metra et pedes ac verborum elegans dispositio et sententiarum inter personas distinctas [versuum] pronuntiatio prolectando sensus legentium perducit sine offensa ad summam scriptorum terminationem.
chunks.traduccion: Those who have expounded their ideas and precepts in more extensive volumes, Emperor, have lent their writings considerable distinction and authority. I too should wish the subject of our studies to permit such expansiveness, so that greater length might enhance the authority of these teachings; but this is less straightforward than one might suppose. Architecture cannot be written about in the same way as history or poetry. History holds the reader’s attention through the prospect of varied new events; poetry, through its meters, rhythms, elegant arrangement of words and speeches assigned to different characters, carries the reader’s attention smoothly to the conclusion of the work.

chunks.texto: id autem in architecturae conscriptionibus non potest fieri, quod vocabula ex artis propria necessitate concepta inconsueto sermone obiciunt sensibus obscuritatem. cum ergo ea per se non sint aperta nec pateant eorum in consuetudine nomina, tum etiam praeceptorum late vagantes scripturae, si non contrahentur, ut paucis et perlucidis sententiis explicentur, frequentia multitudineque sermonis inpediente incertas legentium efficient cogitationes. itaque occultas nominationes commensusque e membris operum pronuntians, ut memoriae tradantur, breviter exponam. sic enim expeditius ea recipere poterunt mentes.
chunks.traduccion: Architectural writing cannot achieve the same effect, because the technical vocabulary required by the art is unfamiliar and difficult for readers. If the exposition also wanders at length instead of being compressed into a few clear statements, the quantity of words will confuse their understanding. I shall therefore explain unfamiliar terms and the measured relationships of architectural members briefly, so that they can be remembered and more readily understood.

chunks.texto: non minus cum animadvertissem distentam occupationibus civitatem publicis et privatis negotiis, paucis iudicavi scribendum, uti angusto spatio vacuitatis ea legentes breviter percipere possent. Etiamque Pythagorae quique eius haeresim fuerunt secuti placuit cybicis rationibus praecepta in voluminibus scribere, constitueruntque cybum CCXVI versus eosque non plus tres in una conscriptione oportere esse putaverunt.
chunks.traduccion: Seeing also that the citizens were occupied with public and private affairs, I judged that I should write briefly, so that they could grasp my subject during their limited leisure. Pythagoras and the followers of his school likewise chose to set down their precepts in books on a cubic principle: they made one cube consist of 216 verses and thought that no more than three such units should appear in a single composition.

chunks.texto: Cybus autem est corpus ex lateribus aequali latitudine planitiarum perquadratum. is cum est iactus, quam in partem incubuit dum est intactus inmotam habet stabilitatem, uti sunt etiam tesserae quas in alveo ludentes iaciunt. hanc autem similitudinem ex eo sumpsisse videntur quod is numerus versuum uti cybus in quemcumque sensum insederit, inmotam efficiat ibi memoriae stabilitatem. Graeci quoque poetae comici interponentes e choro canticum diviserunt spatia fabularum. ita partes cybica ratione facientes intercapedinibus levant actorum pronuntiationes.
chunks.traduccion: A cube is a solid bounded by equal square faces. When thrown, it remains stable on whichever face it rests, provided it is left untouched, like the dice cast by players into a gaming tray. The comparison seems to have been adopted because this number of verses, once established in the mind as a cube rests on a face, would give memory a similar stability. Greek comic poets also divided their plays by inserting songs for the chorus. By organizing the parts on a cubic principle, they relieved the actors’ delivery with intervals.

chunks.texto: Cum ergo haec naturali modo sint a maioribus observata animoque advertam inusitatas et obscuras multis res esse mihi scribendas, quo facilius ad sensus legentium pervenire possint, brevibus voluminibus iudicavi scribere. ita enim expedita erunt ad intellegendum. eorumque ordinationes institui uti non sint quaerentibus separatim colligenda, sed e corpore uno et in singulis voluminibus generum haberent explicationes. itaque, Caesar, tertio et quarto volumine aedium sacrarum rationes exposui, hoc libro publicorum locorum expediam dispositiones. primumque forum uti oporteat constitui dicam, quod in eo et publicarum et privatarum rerum rationes per magistratus gubernantur.
chunks.traduccion: Since our predecessors observed these principles in a natural way, and since I must discuss matters unfamiliar and obscure to many readers, I have chosen to write short books that make them easier to understand. I have arranged the material so that readers need not gather it from separate sources: the work forms a single body, with each book explaining a particular class of subjects. Thus, Caesar, after setting out the principles of sacred buildings in the third and fourth books, I shall explain the arrangement of public places in this one. I shall begin with the forum, where magistrates administer public and private affairs.

chunks.texto: Graeci in quadrato amplissimis et duplicibus porticibus fora constituunt crebrisque columnis et lapideis aut marmoreis epistyliis adornant et supra ambulationes in contignationibus faciunt. Italiae vero urbibus non eadem est ratione faciendum, ideo quod a maioribus consuetudo tradita est gladiatoria munera in foro dari.
chunks.traduccion: The Greeks raised large double porticoes in the agora and adorned them with closely set columns and with epistyles of stone or marble, and above they made walkways over the floors. But in the cities of Italy this should not be done in the same way, because it is a custom handed down by the ancestors to give gladiatorial shows in the forum.

chunks.texto: igitur circum spectacula spatiosiora intercolumnia distribuantur circaque in porticibus argentariae tabernae maenianaque superioribus coaxationibus conlocentur, quae et ad usum et ad vectigalia publica recte erunt disposita. Magnitudines autem ad copiam hominum oportet fieri, ne parvum spatium sit ad usum aut ne propter inopiam populi vastum forum videatur. latitudo autem ita finiatur uti longitudo in tres partes cum divisa fuerit, ex his duae partes ei dentur. ita enim erit oblonga eius formatio et ad spectaculorum rationem utilis dispositio.
chunks.traduccion: Therefore the spaces between the columns around the area used for spectacles should be wider. Bankers’ shops should be arranged in the surrounding porticoes, with viewing galleries on the upper floors, so that the whole serves its intended uses and provides public revenue.

chunks.texto: columnae superiores quarta parte minores quam inferiores sunt constituendae, propterea quod oneri ferendo quae sunt inferiora firmiora debent esse quam superiora, non minus quod etiam nascentium oportet imitari naturam, ut in arboribus teretibus, abiete cupresso pinu, e quibus nulla non crassior est ab radicibus, dein decrescendo progreditur in altitudinem naturali contractura peraequata nascens ad cacumen. ergo si natura nascentium ita postulat, recte est constitutum et altitudinibus et crassitudinibus superiora inferiorum fieri contractiora.
chunks.traduccion: The upper columns should be one-quarter smaller than the lower ones. The members carrying the load below must be stronger, and the arrangement should also follow the growth of trees: fir, cypress and pine are thicker at the roots and narrow naturally toward the top. Since this is the pattern of growth, the upper members are appropriately reduced in both height and thickness.

chunks.texto: Basilicarum loca adiuncta foris quam calidissimis partibus oportet constitui, ut per hiemem sine molestia tempestatium se conferre in eas negotiatores possint. Earumque latitudines ne minus quam ex tertia, ne plus ex dimidia longitudinis constituantur, nisi si loci natura inpedierit et aliter coegerit symmetriam commutari. Sin autem locus erit amplior in longitudine, chalcidica in extremis constituantur, uti sunt in Iulia Aquiliana.
chunks.traduccion: The sites of the basilicas, adjoined to the fora, should be established on the warmest sides, so that in winter the merchants may resort to them without the annoyance of storms. Their widths should be set at no less than a third and no more than half of their length, unless the nature of the site prevents it and compels the symmetry to be otherwise altered. But if the site is more ample in length, let chalcidica be placed at the ends, as they are in the Julia Aquiliana.

chunks.texto: Columnae basilicarum tam altae, quam porticus latae fuerint, faciendae videntur; porticus, quam medium spatium futurum est, ex tertia finiatur. Columnae superiores minores quam inferiores, uti supra scriptum est, constituantur. Pluteum, quod fuerit inter superiores et inferiores columnas, item quarta parte minus, quam superiores columnae fuerint, oportere fieri videtur, uti supra basilicae contignationem ambulantes ab negotiatoribus ne conspiciantur. Epistylia, zophora, coronae ex symmetriis columnarum, uti in tertio libro diximus, explicentur.
chunks.traduccion: The columns of the basilicas appear to be as tall as the width of the portico; the gallery, which will be the space in between, should be completed from the third level. The upper columns should be smaller than the lower ones, as described above. The shelf, which was between the upper and lower columns, also a quarter shorter than the upper columns, seems to have been necessary so as not to be seen by the merchants walking on the basilica floor. The architraves (epistylia), friezes (zophora), and cornices are set out according to the symmetries of the columns, as we said in the third book.

chunks.texto: Non minus summam dignitatem et venustatem possunt habere comparationes basilicarum quo genere Coloniae Iuliae Fanestri conlocavi curavique faciendam, cuius proportiones et symmetriae sic sunt constitutae. mediana testudo inter columnas est longa pedes CXX, lata pedes LX. porticus eius circa testudinem inter parietes et columnas lata pedes XX. columnae altitudinibus perpetuis cum capitulis pedes L, crassitudinibus quinûm, habentes post se parastaticas altas pedes XX, latas pedes II S, crassas I S, quae sustinent trabes in quibus invehuntur porticuum contignationes. supraque eas aliae parastaticae pedum XVIII, latae binûm, crassae pedem, quae excipiunt item trabes sustinentes cantherium et porticûm, quae sunt summissa infra testudinem, tecta.
chunks.traduccion: No less can comparisons of the basilicas of the kind I have placed and taken care to build in the Colonia Julia Fanestri, the proportions and symmetries of which are thus established. The central hall (testudo) between the columns is 120 feet long, 60 feet wide. Its portico around the dome between the walls and columns is 20 feet wide. The columns are of continuous heights with capitals of 50 feet, five feet thick, having behind them parastatics 20 feet high, 25 feet wide, and 15 feet thick, which support the beams on which the floors of the porticoes are carried. And above them other parastatics 18 feet, two feet wide, and a foot thick, which also accommodate the beams supporting the cantherium and the roofs of the porticoes, which are lowered below the dome.

chunks.texto: reliqua spatia inter parastaticarum et columnarum trabes per intercolumnia luminibus sunt relicta. columnae sunt in latitudine testudinis cum angularibus dextra ac sinistra quaternae, in longitudine quae est foro proxima cum isdem angularibus octo, ex altera parte cum angularibus VI, ideo quod mediae duae in ea parte non sunt positae ne inpediant aspectus pronai aedis Augusti, quae est in medio latere parietis basilicae conlocata spectans medium forum et aedem Iovis,
chunks.traduccion: The remaining spaces, between the beams of the pilasters and those of the columns, are left open through the intercolumniations to admit light. Across the width of the nave (testudo) the columns are four on each side, counting the corner ones, right and left; along the long side nearest the forum, eight with the same corner columns; and on the other side, six, because the two central columns were not set on that side, so as not to block the view of the pronaos of the temple of Augustus, which stands in the middle of the basilica’s side wall, facing the center of the forum and the temple of Jupiter.

chunks.texto: item tribunal quod est in ea aede hemicycli schematis minoris curvatura formatum. eius autem hemicycli in fronte est intervallum pedes XLVI, introrsus curvatura pedes XV, uti qui apud magistratus starent negotiantes in basilica ne inpedirent. supra columnas ex tribus tignis bipedalibus compactis trabes sunt circa conlocatae. eaeque ab tertiis columnis quae sunt in interiore parte revertuntur ad antas quae a pronao procurrunt dextraque et sinistra hemicyclium tangunt.
chunks.traduccion: Likewise, the tribunal in that hall is formed with the curvature of a hemicycle of a lesser segment. The front of this hemicycle is forty-six feet across, and its curvature inward fifteen feet, so that those who stood before the magistrates might not obstruct those doing business in the basilica. Above the columns, beams made of three two-foot timbers joined together are placed around; and these, from the third columns which are on the inner side, return to the antae that run forward from the pronaos and touch the hemicycle on the right and left.

chunks.texto: supra trabes contra capitula ex fulmentis dispositae pilae sunt conlocatae altae pedes III, latae quoqueversus quaternis. supra eas ex duobus tignis bipedalibus trabes everganeae circa sunt conlocatae. quibus insuper transtra cum capreolis columnarum contra corpora et antas et parietes pronai conlocata sustinent unum culmen perpetuae basilicae, alterum a medio supra pronaum aedis.
chunks.traduccion: Above the beams, opposite the capitals and set upon brackets, piers (pilae) are placed, three feet high and four feet wide each way. Upon these, made of two two-foot timbers, beams are laid running round about. And upon these, the cross-beams with the struts (capreoli) of the columns, set against the shafts, the antae and the walls of the pronaos, support two ridge-beams: one running the whole length of the basilica, the other rising from the center over the pronaos of the temple.

chunks.texto: ita fastigiorum duplex pectinata dispositio extrinsecus tecti et interioris altae testudinis praestat speciem venustam. item sublata epistyliorum ornamenta et pluteorum columnarumque superiorum distributio operosam detrahit molestiam sumptusque inminuit ex magna parte summam. ipsae vero columnae in altitudine perpetua sub trabes testudinis perductae et magnificentiam inpensae et auctoritatem operi adaugere videntur.
chunks.traduccion: Thus the double arrangement of the roof-pediments, so produced, presents a beautiful appearance both on the exterior of the roof and within the high vaulted nave (testudo). Moreover, the omission of the ornaments of the architraves (epistylia), together with the arrangement of the parapets (plutei) and the upper columns, removes laborious work and greatly reduces the total cost. And the columns themselves, carried up in continuous height to the beams of the vault, seem to add magnificence to the outlay and authority to the work.

chunks.texto: Aerarium, carcer, curia foro sunt coniungenda, sed ita uti magnitudo ⟨ac⟩ symmetriae eorum foro respondeant. maxime quidem curia in primis est facienda ad dignitatem municipii sive civitatis. et si quadrata erit, quantum habuerit latitudinis dimidia addita constituatur altitudo, sin autem oblonga fuerit, longitudo et latitudo componatur et summae compositae, eius dimidia pars sub lacunariis altitudini detur.
chunks.traduccion: The treasury, the prison, and the senate-house (curia) should adjoin the forum, but so that the magnitude of their symmetry answers to the forum. Above all the curia is to be built in keeping with the dignity of the municipality or city. If it is square, let its height be established by adding to its width the half of that width; but if it is oblong, let its length and width be added together, and of that total sum let the half be given to the height, up to the coffered ceiling.

chunks.texto: praeterea praecingendi sunt parietes medii coronis ex intestino opere aut albario ad dimidiam partem altitudinis. quae si non erunt, vox ibi disputantium elata in altitudinem intellectui non poterit esse audientibus. cum autem coronis praecincti parietes erunt, vox ab imis, morata priusquam in aera elata dissipabitur, auribus erit intellecta.
chunks.traduccion: Furthermore, the walls are to be girded at mid-height by cornices of joinery (intestinum opus) or of stucco (albarium). For if these are lacking, the voice of those debating, rising into the height, cannot be understood by the listeners. But when the walls are girded with cornices, the voice, held back from below before it rises into the air and is dissipated, will be understood by the ears.

chunks.texto: Cum forum constitutum fuerit, tum deorum inmortalium diebus festis ludorum spectationibus eligendus est locus theatro quam saluberrimus, uti in primo libro de salubritatibus in moenium conlocationibus est scriptum. per ludos enim cum coniugibus et liberis persedentes delectationibus detinentur et corpora propter voluptatem inmota patentes habent venas, in quas insidunt aurarum flatus, qui si a regionibus palustribus aut aliis regionibus vitiosis advenient, nocentes spiritus corporibus infundent. itaque si curiosius eligetur locus theatro, vitabuntur vitia.
chunks.traduccion: Once the forum was established, then, in anticipation of the festivals of the immortal gods, a place as wholesome as possible should be chosen for the theater, as is written in the first book concerning the healthfulness of settlements within the walls. For during the games, those who sit with their wives and children are seized by pleasure, and their bodies are immobile because of it, and their veins are open, through which gusts of wind enter, which, if they come from marshy or other vicious regions, infuse their bodies with harmful spirits. Therefore, if the place for the theater is chosen with greater care, defects will be avoided.

chunks.texto: etiamque providendum est ne impetus habeat a meridie. sol enim cum implet eius rotunditatem, aer conclusus curvatura neque habens potestatem vagandi versando confervescit et candens adurit excoquitque et inminuit e corporibus umores. ideo maxime vitandae sunt his rebus vitiosae regiones et eligendae salubres.
chunks.traduccion: Care must also be taken that the hall does not receive the southern exposure. For when the sun fills the chamber with its heat, the air enclosed in the vault, having no way to circulate, boils and consumes with its vapor the sturdy parts of the bodies.

chunks.texto: fundamentorum autem, si in montibus fuerint, facilior erit ratio, sed si necessitas coegerit in plano aut palustri loco ea constitui, solidationes substructionesque ita erunt faciendae, quemadmodum de fundationibus aedium sacrarum in tertio libro est scriptum. insuper fundamenta lapideis et marmoreis copiis gradationes ab substructione fieri debent.
chunks.traduccion: But the arrangement of the foundations, if they are in the mountains, will be easier; but if necessity compels them to be established on a plain or in a marshy place, the consolidations and substructures will be made in the same way as is written about the foundations of the sacred buildings in the third book. Moreover, the foundations must be of stone and the steps of marble for the substructure.

chunks.texto: praecinctiones ad altitudines theatrorum pro rata parte faciendae videntur, neque altiores quam quanta praecinctionis itineris sit latitudo. si enim excelsiores fuerint, repellent et eicient e superiore parte vocem nec patientur in sedibus suis, quae sunt supra praecinctiones, verborum casus certa significatione ad aures pervenire. et ad summam ita est gubernandum uti linea cum ad imum gradum et ad summum extenta fuerit, omnia cacumina graduum angulosque tangat. ita vox non inpedietur.
chunks.traduccion: The praecinctiones (belts) should be made in proportion to the height of the theaters, and no higher than the width of the passage of the praecinctio; for if they were too high, they would drive the voice upward and would not let the endings of words reach with clarity the ears of those seated above the praecinctiones. In sum, it must be so governed that, when a line is drawn from the lowest step to the highest, it touches all the summits and angles of the steps: thus the voice will not be hindered.

chunks.texto: aditus complures et spatiosos oportet disponere, nec coniunctos superiores inferioribus sed ex omnibus locis perpetuos et directos sine inversuris faciendos, uti cum populus dimittatur de spectaculis, ne comprimatur, sed habeat ex omnibus locis exitus separatos sine inpeditione. Etiam diligenter est animadvertendum ne sit locus surdus, sed ut in eo vox quam clarissime vagari possit. hoc vero fieri ita poterit, si locus electus fuerit ubi non inpediatur resonantia.
chunks.traduccion: It is necessary to provide several spacious entrances, and not to connect the upper and lower ones, but to make them continuous and direct from all areas without any obstacles, so that when people leave the performances, they should not be cramped, but have separate exits from all areas without obstruction. Care must also be taken to ensure that it is not a soundproof space, but that the voice can travel through it as clearly as possible. This can only be achieved if a location has been chosen where echoes are not lingering.
