Ea translata ex terebratione in terebrationem mensis vertentis perficit cursum suum.
chunks.traduccion: Thus, as much as the scales are lifted from the water, so much does the weight of the ballast below turn the axis, and the axis the drum. The turning of which drum sometimes has an effect, as the greater part of the circle of the standard, sometimes the lesser, in its turnings, designates the properties of the hours. For in each of the signs of each month the numbers of the days are perfected in a hollow, the bubble of which, which seems to hold the image of the sun in clocks, signifies the spaces of the hours. It is translated from one bore to another of the bores of the turning month, and it completes its course.

chunks.texto: Itaque quemadmodum sol per siderum spatia vadens dilatat contrahitque dies et horas, sic bulla in horologiis ingrediens per puncta contra centri tympani versationem, cotidie cum transfertur aliis temporibus per latiora, aliis per angustiora spatia, menstruis finitionibus imagines efficit horarum et dierum.
chunks.traduccion: In the same way, as the sun, as it travels through the spaces of the stars, expands and contracts the days and hours, so the bubble in clocks, entering through points against the rotation of the center of the drum, when it is daily transferred at some times through wider spaces, at others through narrower spaces, produces the monthly endings of the image of the hours and days.

chunks.texto: De administratione autem aquae, quemadmodum se temperet ad rationem, sic erit faciendum. Post frontem horologii intra conlocetur castellum in idque per fistulam saliat aqua et in imo habeat cavum. Ad id autem adfixum sit ex aere tympanum habens foramen, per quod ex castello in id aqua influat. In eo autem minus tympanum includatur cardinibus ex torno masculo et femina inter se coartatis, ita uti minus tympanum quemadmodum epitonium in maiore circumagendo arte leniterque versetur.
chunks.traduccion: The water supply is regulated as follows. Behind the face of the clock place a tank, into which water flows through a pipe, with an opening at its base. Attach to it a bronze drum with an aperture through which water passes from the tank. Fit a smaller drum inside it by accurately turned male and female pivots, so that the smaller drum can rotate smoothly and closely within the larger, like a stopcock.

chunks.texto: Maioris autem tympani labrum aequis intervallis CCCLXV puncta habeat signata, minor vero orbiculus in extrema circinatione fixam habeat lingulam, cuius cacumen dirigat ad punctorum regiones, inque eo orbiculo temperatum sit foramen, quia in tympanum aqua influit per id et servat administrationem. Cum autem in maioris tympani labro fuerint signorum caelestium deformationes, id autem sit inmotum et in summo habeat deformatum cancri signum, ad perpendiculum eius in imo capricorni, ad dextram spectantis librae, ad sinistram arietis signum, ceteraque inter eorum spatia designata sint, uti in caelo videntur.
chunks.traduccion: The lip of the larger drum should have 365 points marked at equal intervals, while the smaller one should have a fixed circle in the outer circumference, the top of which should point to the regions of the points, and in that circle there should be a moderate opening, because water flows into the drum through it and maintains its administration. But since there are deformations of the celestial signs on the lip of the larger drum, it should be immovable and have at the top a deformed sign of Cancer, at its perpendicular at the bottom a Capricorn, to the right a Libra looking at it, to the left a Aries, and the rest should be designated between their spaces, as they appear in the sky.

chunks.texto: Igitur cum sol fuerit in capricorni, orbiculi lingula in maioris tympani parte ex capricorni cotidie singula puncta tangens, ad perpendiculum habens aquae currentis vehemens pondus, celeriter per orbiculi foramen id extrudit ad vasum excipiens eam, cum brevi spatio impletur, corripit et contrahit dierum spatia et horarum. Cum autem cotidiana versatione minoris tympani lingula ingrediatur in aquarii puncta, discedens foramen a perpendiculo et aquae vehementi cursu cogitur tardius emittere salientem. Ita quo minus celeri cursu vas excipit aquam, dilatat horarum spatia.
chunks.traduccion: Therefore, when the sun is in Capricorn, the ligula of the orb, touching each point of the greater drum on the part of Capricorn every day, having the violent weight of the flowing water at a perpendicular, quickly pushes it out through the hole of the orb to the vessel. Then, receiving it, when it is filled in a short time, it contracts and contracts the smaller spaces of the days and hours. But when, by the daily turning of the lesser drum, the ligula enters the points of Aquarius, the holes descend perpendicularly and the violent flow of the water is forced to let out the water more slowly. Thus, the less rapidly the vessel receives the water, the longer the spaces of the hours.

chunks.texto: Aquarii vero pisciumque punctis uti gradibus scandens orbiculi foramen in ariete tangendo octavam partem aqua temperate salienti praestat aequinoctiales horas. Ab ariete per tauri et geminorum spatia ad summa cancri puncta partis octavae foramen se tympani versationibus peragens et in altitudinem eo rediens viribus extenuatur, et ita tardius fluendo dilatat morando spatia et efficit horas in cancri signo solstitiales. A cancro cum proclinat et peragit per leonem et virginem ad librae partis octavae puncta revertendo et gradatim corripiendo spatia contrahit horas, et ita perveniens ad puncta librae aequinoctiales rursus reddit horas.
chunks.traduccion: But the opening of the orb, ascending like steps through the points of Aquarius and Pisces, in Aries, touching the eighth part of the temperately rising water, gives the equinoctial hours. From Aries, through the space of Taurus and Gemini, to the highest points of Cancer, the opening of the eighth part, passing through the turns of a drum, and returning to the height, is weakened by its forces, and thus, flowing more slowly, it expands and lingers the spaces and produces the solstitial hours in the sign of Cancer. From Cancer, when it inclines and passes through Leo and Virgo, to the points of Libra, returning and gradually contracting the spaces, it contracts the hours, and thus arriving at the points of the equinoctial Libra, it again gives the hours.

chunks.texto: Per scorpionis vero spatia et sagittarii proclivius deprimens se foramen rediensque circumactione ad capricorni partem VII, restituit celeritate salientis brumales horarum brevitates.
chunks.traduccion: But through the spaces of Scorpio and the inclined slope of Sagittarius, the opening, lowering itself and returning by rotation to the eighth part of Capricorn, is restored with the speed of the spring to the shortness of the winter hours.

chunks.texto: Nobili Graecorum et ampla civitate Ephesi lex vetusta dicitur a maioribus dura condicione sed iure esse non iniquo constituta. Nam architectus, cum publicum opus curandum recipit, pollicetur, quanto sumptu id sit futurum. Tradita aestimatione magistratui bona eius obligantur, donec opus sit perfectum. Absoluto autem, cum ad dictum inpensa respondit, decretis et honoribus ornatur. Item si non amplius quam quarta, ad aestimationem est adicienda, de publico praestatur, neque ulla poena tenetur. Cum vero amplius quam quarta in opere consumitur, ex eius bonis ad perficiendum pecunia exigitur.
chunks.traduccion: In the great and distinguished Greek city of Ephesus, the ancestors are said to have established an ancient law, severe in its terms yet not unjust. When an architect undertakes a public building, he declares its estimated cost. Once that estimate has been submitted to the magistrate, his property stands as security until the work is complete. If the final expenditure agrees with the estimate, he receives public honors and decrees of recognition. An overrun of no more than one quarter is covered by the public treasury without penalty. If the excess exceeds one quarter, however, the additional money required to complete the work is recovered from the architect’s own property.

chunks.texto: Utinam dii inmortales fecissent, ea lex etiam <> P<> R<> non modo publicis sed etiam privatis aedificiis esset constituta! Namque non sine poena grassarentur inperiti, sed qui summa doctrinarum subtilitate essent prudentes, sine dubitatione profiterentur architecturam, neque patres familiarum inducerentur ad infinitas sumptuum profusiones, ut et e bonis eicerentur, ipsique architecti poenae timore coacti diligentius modum inpensarum ratiocinantes explicarent, uti patres familiarum ad id, quod praeparavissent, seu paulo amplius adicientes, aedificia expedirent. Nam qui quadringenta ad opus possunt parare, si adicient centum, habendo spem perfectionis delectationibus tenentur; qui autem adiectione dimidia aut ampliore sumptu onerantur, amissa spe et inpensa abiecta, fractis rebus et animis desistere coguntur.
chunks.traduccion: Would that the gods had made immortal, that law had been established not only for public but also for private buildings among the Roman people! For the ignorant would not have been able to go about without punishment, but those who were wise in the highest subtlety of doctrines would have professed architecture without hesitation, nor would the heads of families have been led to endless profusions of expense, and so that they might be driven out of their possessions, and the architects themselves, compelled by fear of punishment, would have been more diligent in calculating the amount of expense, so that the heads of families might have prepared for what they had prepared, or by adding a little more, and would have been able to complete the buildings. For those who can prepare four hundred works, if they add a hundred, are bound by the pleasures of having the hope of perfection; but those who, by adding half, are burdened with a larger expense, are forced to desist, having lost hope and wasted their efforts, with their things and spirits broken.

chunks.texto: Nec solum id vitium in aedificiis, sed etiam in muneribus, quae a magistratibus foro gladiatorum scaenisque ludorum dantur, quibus nec mora neque expectatio conceditur, sed necessitas finito tempore perficere cogit, id est sedes spectaculorum velorumque inductiones et ea omnia, quae scaenicis moribus per machinationem ad spectationes populo comparantur. In his vero opus est prudentia diligens et ingenii doctissimi cogitata, quod nihil eorum perficitur sine machinatione studiorumque vario ac sollerti vigore.
chunks.traduccion: The same difficulty arises not only in buildings but also in the public spectacles provided by magistrates: gladiatorial displays in the forum and theatrical games. Such events admit neither postponement nor delay; seating, awnings and the apparatus required by stage practice must all be ready at a fixed time for the public to see. These undertakings demand careful judgment and highly trained ingenuity, for none can be accomplished without machinery and the varied, resourceful application of technical knowledge.

chunks.texto: Igitur quoniam haec ita sunt tradita et constituta, non videtur esse alienum, uti caute summaque diligentia, antequam instituantur opera, eorum expediantur, rationes. Ergo quoniam neque lex neque morum institutio id potest cogere et quotannis et praetores et aediles ludorum causa machinationes praeparare debent, visum mihi est, imperator, non esse alienum, quoniam de aedificiis in prioribus voluminibus exposui, in hoc, quod finitionem summam corporis habet constitutam, quae sint principia machinarum, ordinata praeceptis explicare.
chunks.traduccion: Therefore, since these things have been handed down and established in this way, it does not seem out of place that, before the works are instituted, their reasons should be carefully and diligently explained. Therefore, since neither law nor morals can compel this, and since every year both praetors and aediles must prepare machines for the games, it has seemed to me, emperor, that it is not out of place, since I have explained buildings in previous volumes, to explain, in this respect, that the finality of the body is established, what are the principles of the machines, ordered by precepts.

chunks.texto: Machina est continens e materia coniunctio maximas ad onerum motus habens virtutes. Ea movetur ex arte circulorum rotundationibus, quam Graeci κυκλικὴν κίνησιν appellant. Est autem unum genus scansorium, quod graece ἀκροβατικόν dicitur; alterum spirabile, quod apud eos πνευματικόν appellatur; tertium tractorium, id autem Graeci βαρουλκόν vocitant. Scansorium autem ⟨est, cum⟩ machinae ita fuerint conlocatae, ut ad altitudinem tignis statutis et transversariis conligatis sine periculo scandatur [ad apparatus spectatione]; at spirabile, cum spiritus ex expressionibus inpulsus et plagae vocesque ὀργανικῶς exprimantur;
chunks.traduccion: Apparatus criticus (10.1.1). machina est Budé, Rose: machinae H · coniunctio Budé : coniuncta G · maximas ed. princ. : maxima codd. plerique. Sigla: H = Harleianus 2767; G = Gudianus 69; ed. princ. = editio princeps (Sulpicius, 1486); codd. plerique = most of the codices.

chunks.texto: Tractorium vero, cum onera machinis pertrahuntur, ut ad altitudinem sublata conlocentur. Scansoria ratio non arte sed audacia gloriatur; ea catenationibus [et transversariis et plexis conligationibus] et erismatorum fulturis continentur. Quae autem spiritus potestate adsumit ingressus, elegantes artis subtilitatibus consequetur effectus. tractoria autem maiores et magnificentia plenas habet ad utilitatem opportunitates et in agendo cum prudentia summas virtutes.
chunks.traduccion: The hoisting kind, by contrast, is employed when loads are drawn up by machines and set in place at a height. The method of lifting does not boast of skill but of daring; it is held in place by chains [and transverse and twisted connections] and supports of erismata. But the kind that takes its impulse from the inrush of air under pressure achieves its elegant effects through the refinements of the art. The hoisting kind offers greater opportunities, full of grandeur, for practical use, and the highest excellence when operated with prudence.

chunks.texto: Ex his sunt quae μηχανικῶς alia ὀργανικῶς moventur. Inter machinas et organa id videtur esse discrimen, quod machinae pluribus operis vel vi maiore coguntur effectus habere, uti ballistae torculariorumque prela; organa autem unius operae prudenti tactu perficiunt quod est propositum, uti scorpionis seu anisocyclorum versationes. Ergo et organa et machinarum ratio ad usum sunt necessaria, sine quibus nulla res potest esse non inpedita.
chunks.traduccion: Of these there are those which are moved mechanically, and others organically. There seems to be a difference between machines and organs, that machines are compelled by a greater force to produce effects, as in the case of ballistas and presses; whereas instruments (organa) accomplish their intended purpose by the skilled touch of a single workman, as in the case of the turning of a scorpion or anisocycles. Therefore both organs and the system of machines are necessary for use, without which nothing can be unhindered.

chunks.texto: Omnis autem est machinatio rerum natura procreata ac praeceptrice et magistra mundi versatione instituta. Namque animadvertamus primum et aspiciamus continentem solis, lunae, quinque etiam stellarum, natura machinata versarentur, non habuissemus interdum lucem nec fructûm maturitates. Cum ergo maiores haec ita esse animadvertissent, e rerum natura sumpserunt exempla et ea imitantes inducti rebus divinis commodas vitae perfecerunt explicationes. Itaque comparaverunt ut essent expeditiora, alia machinis et earum versationibus, nonnulla organis, et ita quae animadverterunt ad usum utilia esse studiis artibus, institutis, gradatim augenda doctrinis curaverunt.
chunks.traduccion: All machinery originates in nature, with the revolution of the universe as its teacher and guide. We should first observe the continuous movement of the sun, the moon and the five planets. […] The transmitted sentence is incomplete here; its surviving conclusion connects their motion with the light and ripening of crops available to us. Our predecessors observed these things, took examples from nature and, by imitating them under the guidance of celestial phenomena, developed devices useful in life. They made some tasks easier by machines and their rotations, others by instruments, and gradually improved what they found useful through study, craftsmanship, instruction and systematic knowledge.

chunks.texto: Attendamus enim primum inventum de necessitate, ut vestitus, quemadmodum telarum organicis administrationibus conexus staminis ad subtemen non modo corpora tegendo tueatur, sed etiam ornatus adiciat honestatem. Cibi vero non habuissemus abundantiam, nisi iuga et aratra bubus iumentisque omnibus essent inventa. Sucularumque et prelorum et vectium si non fuisset torculariis praeparatio, neque olei nitorem neque vitium fructum habere potuissemus ad iucunditatem, portationesque eorum non essent, nisi plostrorum seu serracorum per terram, navicularum per aquam inventae essent machinationes.
chunks.traduccion: For let us consider the first invention of necessity, that clothing, as the organic administrations of the looms connect the warp to the warp, not only protects the body by covering it, but also adorns it to add dignity. But we would not have had an abundance of food if yokes and ploughs had not been invented for oxen and all kinds of cattle. And if there had not been the preparation of water-jugs and presses and levers, we could not have had the shine of oil or the fruit of wine for our enjoyment, and their transportation would not have been possible if the mechanisms of carts or saws had not been invented by land, and of boats by water.

chunks.texto: Trutinarum vero librarumque ponderibus examinatio reperta vindicat ab iniquitate iustis moribus vitam. Non minusque sunt innumerabili modo rationes machinationum, de quibus non necesse videtur disputare, quod non sunt ⟨ignotae sed⟩ ad manum cotidianae, ut sunt molae, folles fabrorum, raedae, cisia, torni ceteraque, quae communes ad usum consuetudinibus habent opportunitates. Itaque incipiemus de îs, quae raro veniunt ad manus, ut nota sint, explicare.
chunks.traduccion: But the examination of scales and weights, discovered by the examination of the scales, vindicates life from injustice by righteous conduct. Not less, which are innumerable ways the methods of machinery, about which it seems unnecessary to discuss, when they are at hand in daily use, such as mills, blacksmiths' bellows, carts, saws, lathes, and other things, which have common uses in custom. Therefore, we will begin to explain those which rarely come to hand, so that they may be known.

chunks.texto: Primumque instituemus de îs, quae aedibus sacris ad operumque publicorum perfectionem necessitate comparantur. Quae fiunt ita. Tigna duo ad onerum magnitudinem ratione expediuntur. A capite ea fibula coniuncta et in imo divaricata eriguntur, funibus in capitibus conlocatis et circa dispositis erecta retinentur. alligatur in summo troclea, quem etiam nonnulli rechamum dicunt. In trocleam induntur orbiculi <⟨II⟩> per axiculos versationes habentes. Per orbiculum <summum> traicitur ductarius funis, deinde demittitur et traducitur circa orbiculum trocleae inferioris. Refertur autem ad orbiculum imum trocleae superioris et ita descendit ad inferiorem et in foramine eius religatur. Altera pars funis refertur inter imas machinae partes.
chunks.traduccion: First, we will discuss those that are necessary for the completion of sacred buildings and public works. These are done in this way. Two beams are prepared according to the size of the loads. They are erected with a clamp at the top and spread apart at the bottom, and are held erect by ropes placed at the ends and arranged around them. A pulley is tied at the top, which some also call a recham. Two small circles are put on the pulley, which have turns through the pins. A conductive rope is passed through the <top> circle, then let down and passed around the circle of the lower pulley. It is then brought back to the lower circle of the upper pulley and thus descends to the lower one and is tied back in its hole. The other part of the rope is brought back between the lower parts of the machine.

chunks.texto: In quadris autem tignorum posterioribus, quo loci sunt divaricata, figuntur chelonia, in quae coiciuntur sucularum capita, ut faciliter axes versentur. Eae suculae proxime capita habent foramina bina ita temperata, ut vectes in ea convenire possint. Ad rechamum autem imum ferrei forfices religantur, quorum dentes in saxa forata accommodantur. Cum autem funis habet caput ad suculam religatum et vectes ducentes eam versant, funis <se> involvendo circum suculam extenditur et ita sublevat onera ad altitudinem et operum conlocationes.
chunks.traduccion: But in the rear squares of the timbers, where the places are spread apart, are fixed chelonias, into which the heads of the pulleys are cast, so that the axes can be easily turned. These pulleys have two holes near the heads so sized that the bars can fit in them. And to the lower recham are tied iron scissors, the teeth of which fit into the holes in the rocks. But when the rope has its head tied to the pulley and the bars that guide it turn it, the rope is stretched by wrapping itself around the pulley and thus raises the height of the load and the placement of the works.

chunks.texto: Haec autem ratio machinationis, quod per tres orbiculos circumvolvitur, trispastos appellatur. Cum vero in ima troclea duo orbiculi, in superiore tres versantur, id pentaspaston dicitur. Sin autem maioribus oneribus erunt machinae comparandae, amplioribus tignorum longitudinibus et crassitudinibus erit utendum; ⟨et⟩ eadem ratione in summo fibulationibus, in imo sucularum versationibus expediendum. His explicatis antarii funes ante laxi conlocentur; retinacula super scapulas machinae longe disponantur, et si non erit, ubi religetur, pali resupinati defodiantur et circum fistucatione solidentur, quo funes alligentur.
chunks.traduccion: This method of working, which is carried out by three small wheels, is called trispastos. But when two small wheels are turned on the lower pulley and three on the upper one, it is called pentaspaston. But if the machine is to be used for greater loads, greater lengths and thicknesses of timbers must be used; in the same way, it must be facilitated by means of fastenings at the top and turning of the pulleys at the bottom. When these are unfolded, the ropes of the antarium are placed loose in front; the ties are arranged far above the shoulders of the machine, and if there is none, where it is to be tied, stakes are sunk in and made firm around by ramming, so that the ropes may be made fast to them.

chunks.texto: Troclea in summo capite machinae rudenti contineatur, et ex eo funis perducatur ad palum et quae est in palo trocleam inligata. Circa eius orbiculum funis indatur et referatur ad eam trocleam, quae erit ad caput machinae religata. Circum autem orbiculum ab summo traiectus funis descendat et redeat ad suculam, quae est in ima machina, ibique religetur. Vectibus autem coacta ⟨cum⟩ sucula versabitur, eriget per se machinam sine periculo. Ita circa dispositis funibus et retinaculis in palis haerentibus ampliore modo machina conlocabitur. Trocleae et ductarii funes, uti supra scriptum est, expediuntur.
chunks.traduccion: The pulley is held at the top of the machine by a rope, and from it the rope is led to the stake and the stake is tied to the pulley. The rope is placed around its circle and brought back to the pulley, which will be tied to the head of the machine. Then, having passed around the circle from the top, the rope is lowered and returns to the pulley, which is at the bottom of the machine, and there it is tied. The pulley, however, being constrained by the bars, will turn and raise the machine by itself without danger. Thus, having placed the ropes and the ties attached to the stakes in a more spacious way, the machine will be placed. The pulleys and the guide ropes, as written above, are prepared.

chunks.texto: Sin autem colossicotera amplitudinibus et ponderibus onera in operibus fuerint, non erit suculae committendum, sed quemadmodum sucula cheloniis retinetur, ita axis includatur habens in medio tympanum amplum, quod nonnulli rotam appellant, Graeci autem ἀμφίεσις, alii περιθήκιον vocant.
chunks.traduccion: But if there are loads of colossal size and weight in the works, the pulley should not be entrusted, but just as the pulley is held in place by a chelonian, it should be enclosed in a wheel having a large drum in the middle, which some call a wheel, but the Greeks call it an amphièsis, and others a perithekion.

chunks.texto: In his autem machinis trocleae non eodem sed alio modo comparantur. Habent enim et in imo et in summo duplices ordines orbiculorum. Ita funis ductarius traicitur in inferioris trocleae foramen, uti aequalia duo capita sint funis, cum erit extensus, ibique secundum inferiorem trocleam resticula circumdata et contenta utraeque partes funis continentur, ut neque <in dextram neque> in sinistram partem possint prodire. Deinde capita funis referuntur in summa troclea ab exteriore parte et deiciuntur circa orbiculos imos et redeunt ad imum coiciunturque infimae trocleae ad orbiculos ex interiore parte et referuntur dextra sinistra; ⟨et⟩ ad caput circa orbiculos summos redeunt.
chunks.traduccion: In these machines, however, the pulleys are not arranged in the same way but in a different way. For they have double rows of circles at both the bottom and the top. The cable is thus passed into the hole of the lower pulley, so that the two ends of the cable are equal when it is extended, and there, according to the lower pulley, the small ropes are surrounded and contained, and both parts of the cable are held, so that they cannot protrude either to the right or to the left. Then the ends of the cable are brought to the outer side of the upper pulley and are thrown around the lower circles and return to the bottom. The lowest pulleys are thrown to the circles from the inner side and are brought back to the right and left; they return to the head around the upper circles.

chunks.texto: Traiecti autem ab exteriore parte feruntur dextra sinistra tympanum in axe ibique, ut haereant, conligantur. Tum autem circa tympanum involutus alter funis refertur ad ergatam, et is circumactus tympanum et axem. Se involvendo pariter extendunt, et ita leniter levant onera sine periculo. Quodsi maius tympanum conlocatum aut in medio aut in una parte extrema fuerit sine ergata, ⟨per⟩ calcantes homines expeditiores habere poterit operis effectus.
chunks.traduccion: Now, having been carried from the outside, they are carried on the right and left sides of the drum on the axle, and there, so that they stick, they are tied together. Then, another rope, wound around the drum, is brought back to the hoist, and this, wound around the drum and the axle. By wrapping themselves together, they stretch equally, and thus gently lift the loads without danger. But if a larger drum is placed either in the middle or on one of the extreme sides without being hoisted, the men treading will be able to achieve more expeditious results of the work.

chunks.texto: Est autem aliud genus machinae satis artificiosum et ad usum celeritatis expeditum, sed in eo dare operam non possunt nisi periti. Est enim tignum, quod erigitur et distenditur retinaculis quadrifariam. Sub retinaculo chelonia duo figuntur, troclea funibus supra chelonia religatur, sub troclea regula longa circiter pedes duos, lata digitos sex, crassa quattuor supponitur. Trocleae ternos ordines orbiculorum in latitudine habentes conlocantur. Ita tres ductarii funes in ⟨summa⟩ machina religantur. Deinde referuntur ad imam trocleam et traiciuntur ex interiore parte per eius orbiculos summos. Deinde referuntur ad superiorem trocleam et traiciuntur ab exteriore parte in interiorem per orbiculos imos.
chunks.traduccion: There is another kind of machine, however, which is quite ingenious and suitable for rapid use, but only experts can work on it. For it is a beam which is erected and stretched in four ways with ropes. Under the ropes two pulleys are fixed, a pulley is tied with ropes above the pulleys, and under the pulley a rule about two feet long, six fingers wide, and four inches thick is placed. The pulleys are arranged in three rows of circles in width. Thus three guide ropes are tied in the machine. Then they are brought back to the lowest pulley and passed from the inner side through its upper circles. Then they are brought back to the upper pulley and passed from the outer side to the inner side through the lower circles.

chunks.texto: Cum descenderint ad imum, ex interiore parte et per secundos orbiculos traducuntur in extremum et referuntur in summum ad orbiculos secundos; traiecti redeunt ad imum et ab imo referuntur ad caput; traiecti per summos redeunt ad machinam imam. In radice autem machinae conlocatur tertia troclea; eam autem Graeci ἐπάγοντα nostri artemonem appellant. Ea troclea religatur ad trocleae radicem habens orbiculos tres, per quos traiecti funes traduntur hominibus ad ducendum. Ita tres ordines hominum ducentes sine ergata celeriter onus ad summum perducunt.
chunks.traduccion: When they have descended to the bottom, they are carried from the inner side and through the second orbs to the extreme and are brought back to the top to the second orbs; having passed through they return to the bottom and through the bottom they are brought back to the head; having passed through the top they return to the lowest machine. Now at the root of the machine a third pulley is placed; and our Greeks call it the ἐπάγοντα artemon. That pulley is tied to the root of the pulley, having three orbs, through which the ropes are passed and handed over to the men to lead. Thus three ranks of men leading without lifting quickly bring the load to the top.

chunks.texto: Hoc genus machinae polyspaston appellatur, quod multis orbiculorum circumitionibus et facilitatem summam praestat et celeritatem. una autem statutio tigni hanc habet utilitatem, quod ante quantum velit et dextra ac sinistra ab latere proclinando onus deponere potest.
chunks.traduccion: This type of machine is called a polyspaston, which provides both great ease and speed in the many orbits of the wheels. The unique arrangement of the beam has this advantage, that by tilting it forward as much as he wishes and to the right or left side, he can set down the load.

chunks.texto: Non est autem alienum etiam Chersiphronos ingeniosam rationem exponere. Is enim scapos columnarum e lapidicinis cum deportare vellet Ephesi ad Dianae fanum, propter, magnitudinem onerum et viarum campestrem mollitudinem non confisus carris, ne rotae devorarentur, sic est conatus. De materia trientali scapos quattuor, duos transversarios interpositos, quanta longitudo scapi fuerat, complectit et compegit et ferreos cnodacas uti subscudes in capitibus scaporum inplumbavit et armillas in materia ad cnodacas circumdandos infixit;; cnodaces autem in armillis inclusi liberam habuerunt versationem iamiam; ita, cum boves ducerent subiuncti, scapi versando in cnodacibus et armillis sine fine volvebantur.
chunks.traduccion: It is not out of place to set forth the ingenious method of Chersiphron as well. When he wished to convey the shafts of the columns from the quarries to the temple of Diana at Ephesus, he put no faith in carts — for, given the great weight of the loads and the softness of the level roads, he feared the wheels would be swallowed up. He therefore made trial of this device. He took four lengths of timber, each a third of a foot thick, framing two of them as cross-pieces the length of a shaft, and fastened them together; into the ends of the shaft he leaded iron pivots (cnodaces), like dovetail-tenons, and fixed iron rings in the timber to encircle the pivots; the ends, moreover, he secured with wooden cheek-pieces. The pivots, enclosed within the rings, had free play; and so, when the yoked oxen drew the frame, the shafts revolved without end upon their pivots and rings.

chunks.texto: Cum autem scapos omnes ita vexerant et instabant epistyliorum vecturae, filius Chersiphronos Metagenes transtulit ex scaporum vectura etiam in epistyliorum deductione. Fecit enim rotas circiter pedum duodenûm et epistyliorum capita in medias rotas inclusit; item bucculis ligneis capita religavit eadem ratione cnodaces in capitibus armillis inclusit: ita cum trientes a bubus ducerentur, in armillis inclusi cnodaces versabant rotas, epistylia vero inclusa uti axes in rotis eadem ratione, qua scapi, sine mora ad opus pervenerunt. Exemplar autem erit eius, quemadmodum in palaestris cylindri exaequant ambulationes. Neque hoc potuisset fieri, nisi primum propinquitas esset -- non enim plus sunt ab lapidicinis ad fanum milia passuum octo -- nec ullus est clivus sed perpetuus campus.
chunks.traduccion: When all the shafts had been thus conveyed and the transport of the architraves (epistyles) was now pressing, Metagenes, the son of Chersiphron, carried his method over from the moving of the shafts to the moving of the architraves. He made wheels about twelve feet high and enclosed the ends of the architraves within the wheels; in the same way he set pivots and rings into their ends. Thus, when the frames were drawn by oxen, the pivots enclosed in the rings turned the wheels, while the architraves, enclosed like axles within the wheels in the same manner as the shafts, reached the site without delay. A parallel may be seen in the way that rollers level the walks in the palaestrae. Nor could this have succeeded but for the nearness of the place — for it is no more than eight miles from the quarries to the temple — and there is no slope, but a continuous plain.

chunks.texto: Nostra vero memoria cum colossici Apollinis in fano basis esset a vetustate diffracta, et metuentes, ne caderet ea statua et frangeretur, locaverunt ex eisdem lapidicinis basim excidendam. Conduxit quidam Paconius. Haec autem basis erat longa pedes duodecim, lata pedes VIII, alta pedes sex. Quam Paconius gloria fretus non uti Metagenes adportavit, sed eadem ratione alio genere constituit machinam facere.
chunks.traduccion: But our memory is that when the base of the colossal Apollo in the temple was broken by age, and fearing that the statue would give way and break, they hired a base to be cut out of the same stones. A certain Paconius hired it. Now this base was twelve feet long, eight feet wide, and six feet high. Which Paconius, trusting in his fame, did not bring to Metagenes, but for the same reason decided to make a machine of a different kind.

chunks.texto: Rotas enim circiter pedum XV fecit et in his rotis capita lapidis inclusit, deinde circa lapidem fusos sextantales ab rota ad rotam ad circinum compegit, ita uti fusus a fuso non distaret pedem esse unum. Deinde circa fusos funem involvit et bubus iunctis funem ducebant. Ita cum explicaretur, volvebat rotas, sed non poterat ad lineam via recta ducere, sed exibat in unam partem. Ita necesse erat rursus retroducere. Sic Paconius ducendo et reducendo pecuniam contricavit, ut ad solvendum non esset.
chunks.traduccion: For he made wheels about fifteen feet long and enclosed stone heads in these wheels, then he fastened sextantal spindles around the stone from the wheel and the wheel to the compass, so that the spindle was not one foot away from the spindle. Then he wrapped a rope around the spindles and yoked oxen to lead the rope. Thus, when it was unwound, he turned the wheels, but he could not lead them to a straight line, but they went out in one direction. Thus it was necessary to lead them back again. Thus, by leading and bringing them back, Paconius crushed the money, so that there was no way to pay it off.

chunks.texto: Pusillum extra progrediar et de his lapidicinis, quemadmodum sint inventae, exponam. Pixodarus fuerat pastor. Is in his locis versabatur. Cum autem cives Ephesiorum cogitarent fanum Dianae ex marmore facere decernerentque, a Paro, Proconnenso, Heraclea, Thaso uti marmor peteretur, propulsis ovibus Pixodarus in eodem loco pecus pascebat, ibique duo arietes inter se concurrentes alius alium praeterierunt et impetu facto unus cornibus percussit saxum, ex quo crusta candidissimo colore fuerat deiecta. Ita Pixodarus dicitur oves in montibus reliquisse et crustam cursim Ephesum, cum maxime de ea re ageretur, detulisse. Ita statim honores decreverunt ei et nomen mutaverunt: pro Pixodaro Euangelus nominaretur. Hodieque quotmensibus magistratus in eum locum proficiscitur et ei sacrificium facit, et si non fecerit, poena tenetur.
chunks.traduccion: I will go a little further and explain how these stones were found. Pixodarus was a shepherd. He lived in these places. But when the citizens of Ephesus were thinking of building a temple to Diana out of marble and were deciding to do so, and marble was sought from Paros, Proconnesus, Heraclea, and Thasos, Pixodarus, having driven away his sheep, was grazing his flock in the same place, and there two rams, running towards each other, passed each other, and in making a rush, one struck a rock with its horns, from which a crust of the whitest color had fallen. Thus Pixodarus is said to have left the sheep in the mountains and to have carried the crust to Ephesus, when the matter was most discussed. Thus they immediately bestowed honors on him and changed his name: he was to be named Evangelos in place of Pixodarus. And today every month a magistrate goes to that place and makes a sacrifice to it, and if he does not, he is liable to punishment.

chunks.texto: De tractoriis rationibus quae necessaria putavi, breviter exposui. Quorum motus et virtutes duae res diversae et inter se dissimiles ⟨efficiunt⟩, ubi congruentes uti principia pariunt eos perfectus: una porrecti, quam Graeci εὐθεῖαν vocitant, altera rotunditatis, quam Graeci κυκλωτήν appellant. Sed vero neque sine rotunditate motus porrecti nec sine porrecto rotationis versationes onerum possunt facere levationes.
chunks.traduccion: I have briefly explained the principles of traction, which I thought necessary. The movements and powers of which are two things, diverse and dissimilar to each other, as well as congruent as principles, give rise to them in perfection: one of extension, which the Greeks call εὐθεῖαν, the other of rotation, which the Greeks call κυκλωτήν. But neither without rotation can extension movements, nor without extension, can rotations of rotation produce lifting of loads.

chunks.texto: Id autem ut intellegatur, exponam. Inducuntur uti centra axiculi in orbiculos et in trocleis conlocantur, per quos orbiculos funis circumactus directis ductionibus et in sucula conlocatus vectium versationibus onerum facit egressus in altum. Cuius suculae cardines uti centra porrecti in cheloniis, foraminibusque eius vectes conclusi capitibus ad circinum circumactis torni ratione versando faciunt oneris elationes. Quemadmodum etiam ferreus vectis cum est admotus ad onus, quod manuum multitudo non potest movere, supposita uti centro ⟨ultro⟩ citro porrecta pressione, quod Graeci ὑπομόχλιον appellant, et lingua sub onus subdita, caput eius unius hominis viribus pressum id onus extollit.
chunks.traduccion: But that this may be understood, I will explain. They are introduced as centripetals into the orbs and placed in pulleys, through which the rope, wound around the orbs by direct conductions and placed in the pulleys, by the turning of the levers, causes the load to rise upwards. The pivots of which pulleys, like centers extended in the shells, and the levers closed in the holes, with their heads turned around to a compass, cause the load to rise by turning in a manner similar to a turning wheel. Just as when an iron bar is brought near to a load, which a multitude of hands cannot move, if a pressure is placed like a centripetal extended pressure, which the Greeks call ὑπομόχλιον, and the tongue is subjected to the load, its head, pressed by the strength of one man, lifts that load.

chunks.texto: Id autem ⟨eo facilius fit⟩, quo brevior pars prior vectis ab ea pressione, quod est centrum, subit sub onus, et quo longius ab eo centro distans caput eius deducitur. Per id faciundo motus circinationis cogit pressionibus examinare paucis manibus oneris maximi pondus. Item si sub onus vectis ferrei lingula subiecta fuerit neque eius caput pressione in imum, sed adversus in altitudinem extolletur, lingula fulta in areae solo habebit eam pro onere, oneris autem ipsius angulum pro pressione. Ita non tam faciliter quam per oppressionem, sed adversus nihilominus pondus oneris erit excitatum. Igitur si plus lingula vectis supra hypomochlion posita sub onus subierit et caput eius propius centrum pressiones habuerit, non poterit onus elevare, nisi, quemadmodum supra scriptum est, examinatio vectis longitudinis per caput neque ⟨in imum⟩ ductionibus fuerit facta.
chunks.traduccion: For the shorter the distance from the point of pressure, which serves as the center, to the head of the bar where the load is laid, the more easily the weight is raised; and the farther from that center, the harder. Thus the circular movement about the fulcrum allows the heaviest of loads to be lifted by the pressure of but a few hands. And if an iron bar is set beneath a load and its head, rather than being borne downward, is raised upward against the weight, then the bar, resting upon the ground, will take the load as its burden and the very edge of the load as its fulcrum; in this way, though not so readily as by direct downward pressure, it will nonetheless prevail against the weight. Hence, if the bar laid upon the fulcrum has its head set with the pressure too near the center, it will not raise the load; the purchase must be taken, as was said above, along the length of the bar at its head.

chunks.texto: Id autem ex trutinis, quae staterae dicuntur, licet considerare. Cum enim ansa propius caput, unde lancula pendet, ibi ut centrum est conlocata et aequipondium in alteram partem scapi, per puncta vagando quo longius paulatim ad extremum perducitur, paulo et inpari pondere amplissimam pensionem parem perficit per scapi librationem, et examinato longius ab centro recedens ista inbecillior. Aequipondii brevitas maiorem vim ponderis momento deducens sine vehementia molliter ab imo susum versum egredi cogit futurum.
chunks.traduccion: The same may be observed in the balance that is called a steelyard (statera). When the loop from which the beam hangs is set nearer the head — that point serving as the center — and the counterweight (aequipondium) is moved along the other arm, traveling through the farther points or to the very end, then a small and unequal weight balances a great load and holds the beam level; for the counterpoise, as it withdraws further from the center, raises by a gentle pull what at the center would demand a far greater force, drawing the load smoothly upward from below, without violence.

chunks.texto: Quemadmodum etiam navis onerariae maximae gubernator ansam gubernaculi tenens, qui οἴαξ a Graecis appellatur, una manu momento per centrum ratione pressionibus aptis agitans, versat eam amplissimis et inmanibus mercis et penus ponderibus oneratam. Eiusque vela cum sunt per altitudinem mediam mali pendentia, non potest habere navis celerem cursum, cum autem in summo cacumine antemnae subductae sunt, tunc vehementiore progreditur impetu, quod non proxime calcem mali, quod est loco centri, sed in summo longius et ab eo progressa recipiunt in se vela ventum.
chunks.traduccion: Just as the helmsman of a large cargo ship, holding the rudder handle, which the Greeks call oiax, and driving it with one hand at a moment's notice through the center by means of the pressure of the craft, turns it, loaded with the most extensive and enormous cargo and pine weights. And when its sails are suspended along the middle of the mast, the ship cannot have a rapid course, but when the foresails are drawn back at the highest point, then it advances with a more vigorous force, because it does not approach the mast's heel, which is in the place of the center, but at the top, further away, and having advanced from it, the sails receive the wind.

chunks.texto: Itaque uti vectis sub onere subiectus, si per medium premitur, durior est neque incumbit, cum autem caput eius summum deducitur, faciliter onus extollit, similiter vela, cum sunt per medium temperata, minorem habent virtutem, quae autem in capite mali summo conlocantur discedentia longius a centro, non acriore sed eodem flatu, pressione cacuminis vehementius cogunt progredi navem. Etiam remi circa scalmos strophis religati, cum manibus inpelluntur et reducuntur, extremis progredientibus a centro parmis maris undis spumam inpulsu vehementi protrudunt porrectam navem, secante prora liquoris raritatem.
chunks.traduccion: Therefore, like a bar under a load, if it is pressed in the middle, it is stiffer and does not bend, but when its top is lowered, it easily lifts the load. Similarly, sails, when they are adjusted in the middle, have less strength, but those placed at the top of the mast, moving further away from the center, not with a stronger blow, but with the same pressure from the top, force the ship forward more strongly. Also, the oars, tied around the oars with ropes, when they are pushed and pulled back by the hands, with their ends advancing from the center, push the foam of the sea waves with a strong thrust, pushing the ship outstretched, cutting the rarefaction of the liquid at the bow.

chunks.texto: Onerum vero maxima pondera, cum feruntur a phalangariis hexaphoris et tetraphoris, examinantur per ipsa media centra phalangarum, uti diviso oneris solido pondere certa quadam divisionis ratione aequas partes collis singuli ferant operarii. Mediae enim partes phalangarum, quibus lora tetraphororum invehuntur, clavis sunt finitae, ne labantur in unam partem. Cum enim extra finem centri promoventur, premunt eum locum, ad quem propius accesserunt, quemadmodum in statera pondus, cum examine progreditur ad fines ponderationum.
chunks.traduccion: But the greatest weights of burdens, when carried by six- and four-legged phalanxes, are examined through the very middle centers of the phalanxes, so that in a solid weight of the burden divided by a certain ratio of division, each worker may bear an equal part of the load. For the middle parts of the phalanxes, by which the straps of the four-legged phalanxes are carried, are ended with nails, and do not slip to one side. For when they are advanced beyond the end of the center, they press on the place to which they have approached nearest, just as a weight in a balance, when examined, advances to the ends of the weights.

chunks.texto: Eadem ratione iumenta, cum iuga eorum subiugiis loris per medium temperantur, aequaliter trahunt onera. Cum autem inpares sunt eorum virtutes et unum plus valendo premit alterum, loro traiecto fit una pars iugi longior, quae inbecilliori auxiliatur iumento. Ita in phalangis et iugis cum in medio lora non sunt conlocata sed in una parte, qua progreditur lorum ab medio, unam breviorem, <alteram> efficit partem longiorem. Ea ratione si per id centrum, quo loci perductum est lorum, utraque capita circumaguntur, longior pars ampliorem, brevior minorem agit circinationem.
chunks.traduccion: In the same way, when their yokes are controlled by the straps under their yokes in the middle, animals pull loads equally. But when their strengths are unequal and one, being stronger, presses the other, when the strap is passed, one part of the yoke becomes longer, which helps the weaker animal. Thus in phalanxes and yokes, when the straps are not placed in the middle but on one side, where the strap extends from the middle, it makes one part shorter and the other part longer. In the same way, if both ends are driven around the center to which the strap is brought, the longer part makes a greater, the shorter part a smaller, circle.

chunks.texto: Quemadmodum vero minores rotae duriores et difficiliores habent motus, sic phalangae et iuga, in quibus partibus habent minora a centro ad capita intervalla, premunt duriter colla, qua autem longiora habent ab eodem centro spatia, levant oneribus et trahentes et ferentes. Cum haec ita ad centrum porrectionibus et circinationibus reciperent motus, tunc vero etiam plostra, raedae, tympana, rotae, cocleae, scorpiones, ballistae, prela ceteraeque machinae eisdem rationibus per porrectum centrum et rotationem circum versantem faciunt ad propositum effectus.
chunks.traduccion: Just as smaller wheels have harder and more difficult movements, so phalanxes and yokes, in which parts they have smaller distances from the center to the heads, press hard on the necks, while those which have longer distances from the same center lift both those who are pulling and those who are carrying loads. Since these thus receive motions by extension and rotation of the center, then also carts, chariots, drums, wheels, screws, scorpions, ballistas, presses, and other machines, by the same means, produce the intended effects by means of an extended center and the rotation of the compass.

chunks.texto: Nunc de organis, quae ad hauriendam aquam inventa sunt, quemadmodum variis generibus comparentur, exponam. Et primum dicam de tympano. Id autem non alte tollit aquam, sed exhaurit expeditissime multitudinem magnam. Ad tornum aut circinum fabricatus <axis>, capitibus lamna ferratis, habens in medio circa se tympanum ex tabulis inter se coagmentatis, conlocatur in stipitibus habentibus in se sub capita axis ferreas lamminas. In eius tympani cavo interponuntur octo tabulae transversae tangentes axem et extremam tympani circumitionem, quae dividunt aequalia in tympano spatia.
chunks.traduccion: I shall now explain the various kinds of engine devised for drawing water, and how they are severally constructed; and first of the tympanum. This does not raise water to any great height, but it empties out a great quantity with the utmost speed. An axle, turned on the lathe or with the compass and shod with iron at its ends, carries in the middle a drum (tympanum) built up of boards joined together, and rests in blocks that are plated with iron beneath the ends of the axle. Within the hollow of this drum are set eight cross-boards, reaching from the axle to the outer rim and dividing it into equal compartments.

chunks.texto: Circa frontem eius figuntur tabulae, relictis semipedalibus aperturis ad aquam intra concipiendam Item secundum axem columbaria fiunt excavata in singulis spatiis ex una parte. Id autem cum est navali ratione picatum, hominibus calcantibus versatur et hauriendo per aperturas, quae sunt in frontibus tympani, reddit per columbaria secundum axem supposito labro ligneo habente una secum coniunctum canalem. Ita hortis ad inrigandum vel salinis ad temperandum praebetur aquae multitudo.
chunks.traduccion: Boards are fixed around the front, leaving half-foot openings to admit the water. On one side, an outlet resembling a pigeonhole is cut for each compartment next to the axle. The device is waterproofed with pitch like a ship and turned by men treading on it. It draws water through the openings in the face of the drum and discharges it through the outlets by the axle into a wooden trough underneath, fitted with a channel. In this way, large quantities of water are supplied for watering gardens or serving saltworks.

chunks.texto: Sic rota fiet circum axem eadem magnitudine, ut ad altitudinem, quae opus fuerit, convenire possit. Circum extremum latus rotae figentur modioli quadrati pice et cera solidati. Ita cum rota a calcantibus versabitur, modioli pleni ad summum elati rursus ad imum revertentes infundent in castellum ipsi per se quod extulerint.
chunks.traduccion: The wheel is to be made of a size suited to the height of the lift required. Around its outer rim are fastened small square boxes, made watertight with pitch and wax. Thus, when the wheel is turned by treading, the full boxes, carried to the top, return again to the bottom, pouring of their own accord into the reservoir (castellum) what they have brought up.

chunks.texto: Sin autem magis altis locis erit praebendum, in eiusdem rotae axe involuta duplex ferrea catena demissaque ad imum libramentum conlocabitur, habens situlos pendentes aereos congiales. Ita versatio rotae catenam in axem involvendo efferet situlos in summum, qui <cum> super axem pervehuntur, cogentur inverti et infundere in castellum aquae quod extulerint.
chunks.traduccion: But if water is to be supplied at a greater height, a double iron chain is fitted around the axle of the same wheel and let down to the level of the water, carrying bronze buckets hung upon it. Then the turning of the wheel, winding the chain about the axle, raises the buckets to the top; and as they pass over the axle they are tipped, and pour into the reservoir the water they have drawn up.

chunks.texto: Fiunt etiam in fluminibus rotae eisdem rationibus, quibus supra scriptum est. Circa earum frontes adfiguntur pinnae, quae, cum percutiuntur ab impetu fluminis, cogunt progredientes versari rotam, et ita modiolis haurientes et in summum referentes sine operarum calcatura ipsius fluminis inpulsu versatae praestant, quod opus est ad usum.
chunks.traduccion: Wheels are also set up in rivers, on the same principles as those described above. Around their rims are fixed paddles which, struck by the current, drive the wheel round as they are forced along; and so, taking up water in the buckets and carrying it to the top, they accomplish what is required by the river’s own force, without the treading of workmen.

chunks.texto: Eadem ratione etiam versantur hydraletae, in quibus eadem sunt omnia, praeterquam quod in uno capite axis tympanum dentatum est inclusum. Id autem ad perpendiculum conlocatum in cultrum versatur cum rota pariter. Secundum id tympanum maius ⟨minus⟩ item dentatum planum est conlocatum, quo continetur * * *. Ita dentes tympani eius, quod est in axe inclusum, inpellendo dentes tympani plani cogunt fieri molarum circinationem. In qua machina inpendens infundibulum subministrat molis frumentum et eadem versatione subigitur farina.
chunks.traduccion: Water mills, or hydraletae, are turned in the same way. Their construction is similar, except that a toothed drum is fixed to one end of the axle. Set vertically on edge, it turns with the waterwheel. Beside it lies another toothed drum, described as larger, with ⟨smaller⟩ supplied in the printed Latin. [A lacuna follows the clause concerning its support.] The teeth of the drum fixed to the axle drive those of the horizontal drum and cause the millstones to revolve. A hopper suspended above feeds grain to the millstones, and the same rotation grinds it into flour.

chunks.texto: Est autem etiam cocleae ratio, quae magnam vim haurit aquae, sed non tam alte tollit quam rota. Eius autem ratio sic expeditur. Tignum sumitur, cuius tigni quanta paratur pedum longitudo, tanta digitorum expeditur crassitudo. Id ad circinum rotundatur. In capitibus circino dividentur circumitiones eorum tetrantibus et octantibus in partes octo, eaeque lineae ita conlocentur, ut plano posito tigno utriusque capitis ad libellam lineae inter se respondeant, et quam magna pars sit octava circinationis tigni, tam magna spatia decidantur in longitudinem. Item tigno plano conlocato lineae ab capite ad alterum caput perducantur ad libellam convenientes. Sic et in rotundatione et in longitudine aequalia spatia fient. Ita quo loci describuntur lineae, quae sunt in longitudinem spectantes, facient decusationes et in decusationibus finita puncta.
chunks.traduccion: There is also the water screw, or coclea, which raises a large volume of water, though not as high as a wheel. Its construction is as follows. Take a timber whose thickness in digits has the same numerical value as its length in feet, and round it to a cylinder. With compasses, divide the circumference at each end into eight equal parts, first quartering and then bisecting the quarters. Lay the timber horizontally so that the corresponding divisions at its two ends are level. Along its length, mark intervals equal to one-eighth of its circumference. Draw longitudinal lines connecting corresponding divisions at the ends. The divisions around the timber and along its length will thus be equal, and the intersecting lines will provide the points required for the construction.

chunks.texto: His ita emendate descriptis sumitur salignea tenuis aut de vitice secta regula, quae uncta liquida pice figitur in primo decusis puncto. Deinde traicitur oblique ad insequentis longitudinis et circumitionis decusis, item ex ordine progrediens singula puncta praetereundo et circum involvendo conlocatur in singulis decusationibus, et ita pervenit et figitur ad eam lineam recedens a primo in octavum punctum, in qua prima pars est eius fixa. Eo modo quantum progreditur oblique spatium et per octo puncta, tantundem et longitudine procedit ad octavum punctum. Eadem ratione per omne spatium longitudinis et rotunditatis singulis decusationibus oblique fixae regulae per octo crassitudinis divisiones involutos faciunt canales et iustam cocleae naturalemque imitationem.
chunks.traduccion: Once the layout has been accurately marked, take a thin strip of willow or cut osier, coat it with liquid pitch and fix it at the first intersection. Carry it obliquely to the next intersection along the timber and around its circumference. Continue in sequence from point to point, winding the strip around the timber and fixing it at each crossing, until it returns to the longitudinal line on which it began, at the eighth point. In passing obliquely through eight points around the circumference, it also advances eight divisions along the length. Continue this construction throughout the timber, fixing the strips obliquely at successive intersections. Winding through the eight divisions produces channels that reproduce the natural form of a spiral shell.

chunks.texto: Ita per id vestigium aliae super alias figuntur unctae pice liquida, et exaggerantur ad id, uti longitudinis octava pars fiat summa crassitudo. Supra eas circumdantur et figuntur tabulae, quae pertegant eam involutionem. Tunc eae tabulae pice saturantur et lamminis ferreis conligantur, ut ab aquae vi ne dissolvantur. Capita tigni ferrea. Dextra autem ac sinistra cocleam tigna conlocantur in capitibus utraque parte habentia transversaria confixa. In his foramina ferrea sunt inclusa inque ea inducuntur styli, et ita cocleae hominibus calcantibus faciunt versationes.
chunks.traduccion: Following the same tracks, fix further strips over the first, coating them with liquid pitch and building them up until the total thickness is one-eighth of the length. Enclose the winding construction with boards, saturate these with pitch and bind them with iron bands so that the pressure of the water cannot force them apart. Fit iron ends to the central timber. Place supporting timbers on either side of the screw, with crosspieces fixed at both ends. Iron bearings set into these receive the pivots, allowing the screw to rotate when operated by men treading on it.

chunks.texto: Erectio autem eius ad inclinationem sic erit conlocanda, uti, quemadmodum Pythagoricum trigonum orthogonium describitur, sic id habeat responsum, id est uti dividatur longitudo in partes V, earum trium extollatur caput cocleae; ita erit ab perpendiculo ad imas naris spatium earum partium IIII. Qua ratione autem oporteat id esse, in extremo libro eius forma descripta est in ipso tempore.
chunks.traduccion: Set the screw at the inclination of a Pythagorean right triangle: divide its length into five parts and raise its upper end by three of them. The horizontal distance from the foot of the perpendicular to the lower inlet will then be four parts. The arrangement is illustrated by a figure at the end of this book.

chunks.texto: Insequitur nunc de Ctesibica machina, quae in altitudinem aquam educit, monstrare. Ea fit ex aere. Cuius in radicibus modioli fiunt gemelli paulum distantes, habentes fistulas furcillae figura similiter cohaerentes, in medium catinum concurrentes. In quo catino fiunt asses in superioribus naribus fistularum coagmentatione subtili conlocati, qui praeobturantes foramina narium non patiuntur ⟨redire⟩ quod spiritu in catinum est expressum.
chunks.traduccion: There follows the machine of Ctesibius, which raises water to a height. It is made of bronze. At its base are two cylinders (modioli) set a little apart, with pipes joined in the shape of a fork and meeting at a central vessel. In this vessel are fitted valves (asses), carefully placed over the upper mouths of the pipes, which by stopping those openings keep back what has been driven into the vessel under pressure.

chunks.texto: Supra catinum paenula ut infundibulum inversum est attemperata et per fibulam cum catino cuneo traiecto continetur, ne vis inflationis aquae eam cogat elevari. Insuper fistula, quae tuba dicitur, coagmentata in altitudine fit erecta. Modioli autem habent infra nares inferiores fistularum asses interpositos supra foramina eorum, quae sunt in fundis.
chunks.traduccion: A cover shaped like an inverted funnel is fitted above the central vessel and secured to it by a fastening with a wedge driven through, so that the pressure of the water cannot lift it. A pipe called the tuba is joined above it and rises vertically. The cylinders also have valves above the holes in their bottoms, beneath the lower mouths of the pipes.

chunks.texto: Ita de supernis in modiolis emboli masculi torno politi et oleo subacti conclusique regulis et vectibus cum molientur. Qui erit aer ibi cum aqua, assibus obturantibus foramina cogent. et trudent inflando pressionibus per fistularum nares aquam in catinum, e quo recipiens paenula spiritu exprimit per fistulam in altitudinem, et ita ex inferiore loco castello conlocato ad saliendum aqua subministratur.
chunks.traduccion: Pistons, accurately turned on a lathe and lubricated with oil, are inserted into the cylinders from above and operated by rods and levers. As the valves close the openings, the pistons compress the air and water within the cylinders and drive the water under pressure through the mouths of the pipes into the central vessel. The cover receives it and forces it upward through the delivery pipe. In this way, water can be supplied from a reservoir at a lower level to form a fountain jet.

chunks.texto: Nec tamen haec sola ratio Ctesibii fertur exquisita, sed etiam plures et variis generibus ab eo liquore pressionibus coactae spiritus efferre ab natura mutuatos effectus ostenduntur, uti merularum [quae motu] voces atque acrobatae bibentiaque et eadem moventia ⟨se⟩ sigilla ceteraque, quae delectationibus oculorum et aurium usu sensus eblandiantur.
chunks.traduccion: This is not the only device attributed to Ctesibius. Many other inventions of different kinds are said to use air compressed by water to reproduce effects found in nature: the songs of blackbirds, acrobatic figures, little figures that drink and move, and other devices that delight the senses through the pleasures of sight and hearing.

chunks.texto: E quibus quae maxime utilia et necessaria iudicavi selegi, et in priore volumine de horologiis, in hoc de expressionibus aquae dicendum putavi. Reliqua quae non sunt ad necessitatem sed ad deliciarum voluptatem, qui cupidiores erunt eius subtilitatis, ex ipsius Ctesibii commentariis poterunt invenire.
chunks.traduccion: From these inventions I have selected those I judged most useful and necessary. In the preceding book I discussed clocks; in this one, devices for forcing water upward. Readers interested in the ingenious details of inventions made for amusement rather than necessity may consult Ctesibius’s own writings.

chunks.texto: De hydraulis autem, quas habeant ratiocinationes, quam brevissime proximeque attingere potero et scriptura consequi, non praetermittam. De materia compacta basi, ara in ea ex aere fabricata conlocatur. Supra basim eriguntur regulae dextra ac sinistra scalari forma compactae, quibus includuntur aerei modioli, fundulis ambulatilibus ex torno subtiliter subactis habentibus fixos in medio ferreos ancones et verticulis cum vectibus coniunctos, pellibusque lanatis involutis. Item in summa planitia foramina circiter digitorum ternûm. Quibus foraminibus proxime in verticulis conlocati aerei delphini pendentia habent catenis cymbala ex ore infra foramina modiolorum calata.
chunks.traduccion: I shall also explain the principles of water organs as briefly and precisely as a written account allows. An altar-shaped bronze casing is set on a base of joined timber. On either side, ladder-like upright frames hold bronze pump cylinders. Their movable bottoms are accurately turned, wrapped in fleeced skins and fitted at the center with iron elbow pieces jointed to operating levers. In the top surfaces are openings about three digits across. Beside them, bronze dolphins mounted on pivots carry chains in their mouths; cymbal-shaped valves hang from the chains beneath the cylinder openings.

chunks.texto: Intra aram, quo loci aqua sustinetur, inest pnigeus uti infundibulum inversum, quem subter taxilli alti circiter digitorum ternûm suppositi librant spatium imum ima inter labra pnigeos et arae fundum. supra autem cerviculam eius coagmentata arcula sustinet caput machinae, qui graece κανὼν μουσικός appellatur. In cuius longitudine canales, si tetrachordos est, fiunt quattuor, si hexachordos, sex, si octo chordos, octo.
chunks.traduccion: Inside the altar-shaped casing, where the water is held, is a pnigeus shaped like an inverted funnel. Blocks about three digits high support it from below, leaving that clearance between its lower rim and the floor of the casing. Above its neck, a fitted windchest supports the head of the instrument, called the canon musicus (κανὼν μουσικός) in Greek. Along its length there are four channels if the instrument is tetrachord, six if hexachord, and eight if octochord.

chunks.texto: Singulis autem canalibus singula epitonia sunt inclusa, manubriis ferreis conligata. Quae manubria, cum torquentur, ex arca patefaciunt nares in canales. Ex canalibus autem canon habet ordinata in transverso foramina respondentia naribus, quae sunt in tabula summa, quae tabula graece πίναξ dicitur. Inter tabulam et canona regulae sunt interpositae ad eundem modum foratae et oleo subactae, ut faciliter inpellantur et rursus introrsus reducantur, quae obturant ea foramina plinthidesque appellantur. Quarum itus et reditus alias obturat alias aperit terebrationes.
chunks.traduccion: A separate stopcock, or epitonion, is fitted into each channel and connected to an iron handle. Turning the handles opens passages from the windchest into the channels. The canon has transverse rows of holes corresponding to the openings in the upper board, called the pinax (πίναξ). Between the board and the canon lie sliders, similarly pierced and lubricated with oil so that they can move easily inward and outward. These sliders, called plinthides, close or open the holes as they advance and return.

chunks.texto: Haec regulae habent ferrea choragia fixa et iuncta cum pinnis, quarum pinnarum tactus motiones efficit regularum continenter. Supra tabulam foramina ⟨que, per⟩ quae ex canalibus habent egressum spiritus, sunt anuli adglutinati, quibus lingulae omnium includuntur organorum. E modiolis autem fistulae sunt continentes coniunctae pnigeos cervicibus pertinentesque ad nares, quae sunt in arcula. In quibus asses sunt ex torno subacti et ibi conlocati, ⟨ubi fistulae modiolis sunt coniunctae,⟩ qui, cum recepit arcula animam, spiritum non patientur obturantes foramina rursus redire.
chunks.traduccion: Iron linkages fixed to the sliders connect them to the keys; touching the keys moves the sliders in succession. Rings are attached above the openings in the upper board through which air emerges from the channels, and receive the tongues of the organ pipes. Connecting pipes run from the cylinders to the neck of the pnigeus and the openings in the windchest. Turned valves are fitted ⟨where the pipes join the cylinders⟩; once the windchest has received air, these valves close the openings and prevent it from flowing back.

chunks.texto: Ita cum vectes extolluntur, ancones deducunt fundos modiolorum ad imum delphinique, qui sunt in verticulis inclusi, calantes in eos cymbala, aere implent spatia modiolorum, atque ancones extollentes fundos intra modiolos vehementi pulsus crebritate et obturantes foramina cymbalis superiora, aera, qui est ibi inclusus, pressionibus coactum in fistulas cogunt, per quas in pnigea concurrit et per eius cervices in arcam. Motione vero vectium vehementiore spiritus frequens compressus epitoniorum aperturis influit et replet animae canales.
chunks.traduccion: When the levers are raised, the elbow pieces draw the cylinder bottoms downward. The pivoted dolphins lower their cymbal-shaped valves, allowing the cylinders to fill with air. The elbow pieces then drive the bottoms upward with repeated strong strokes. As the valves close the upper openings, the air trapped in the cylinders is compressed and forced through the pipes into the pnigeus and through its neck into the windchest. More vigorous movement of the levers increases the compressed air supply, which passes through the open stopcocks and fills the channels.

chunks.texto: Itaque cum pinnae manibus tactae propellunt et reducunt continenter regulas alternis obturando foramina alternis aperiundo, e musicis artibus multiplicibus modulorum varietatibus sonantes excitant voces.
chunks.traduccion: And so, when the keys (pinnae), pressed by the player’s hands, push the sliders forward and draw them back, by turns closing and opening the holes, they draw from the pipes a rich variety of musical sound, resounding in many melodies.

chunks.texto: Transfertur nunc cogitatio scripturae ad rationem non inutilem sed summa sollertia a maioribus traditam, qua in via raeda sedentes vel mari navigantes scire possimus, quot milia numero itineris fecerimus. Hoc autem erit sic. Rotae, quae erunt in raeda, sint latae per medium diametrum pedum quaternûm [et sextantes], ut, cum finitum locum habeat in se rota ab eoque incipiat progrediens in solo viae facere versationem, perveniendo ad eam finitionem, a qua coeperit versari, certum modum spatii habeat peractum pedes XII s<>.
chunks.traduccion: I now turn to a device of no little usefulness, bequeathed by our forebears with the greatest ingenuity, whereby a man seated in his carriage upon the road, or sailing at sea, may learn how many miles he has traveled. It is contrived thus. The wheels of the carriage are to be four feet in diameter, so that, a fixed point being marked upon one wheel where it first meets the surface of the road, when it returns to that same point in its revolution it will have measured out a definite distance of twelve feet and a half.

chunks.texto: His ita praeparatis tunc in rotae modiolo ad partem interiorem tympanum stabiliter includatur habens extra frontem suae rotundationis extantem denticulum unum. Insuper autem ad capsum raedae loculamentum firmiter figatur habens tympanum versatile in cultro conlocatum et in axiculo conclusum, in cuius tympani fronte denticuli perficiantur aequaliter divisi numero quadringenti convenientes denticulo tympani inferioris. Praeterea superiori tympano ad latus figatur alter denticulus prominens extra dentes.
chunks.traduccion: Having thus prepared these things, a drum is then firmly enclosed in the inner part of the wheel hub, having one denticle protruding beyond the front of its rounding. Moreover, a slot is firmly fixed to the carriage box, having a revolving drum placed in a knife and enclosed in a shaft, into the front of which drum are made denticles evenly divided into four hundred corresponding denticles of the lower drum. Furthermore, another denticle protruding beyond the teeth is fixed to the side of the upper drum.

chunks.texto: Super autem, ⟨tympanum⟩ planum eadem ratione dentatum inclusum in altero loculamento conlocetur, convenientibus dentibus denticulo, qui in secundi tympani latere fuerit fixus, in eoque tympano foramina fiant, quantum diurni itineris miliariorum numero cursus raedae possit exire. Minus plusve rem nihil inpedit. Et in his foraminibus omnibus calculi rotundi conlocentur, inque eius tympani theca, sive id loculamentum est, fiat foramen unum habens canaliculum, qua calculi, qui in eo tympano inpositi fuerint, cum ad eum locum venerint, in raedae capsum et vas aeneum, quod erit suppositum, singuli cadere possint.
chunks.traduccion: Above, however, a plane, toothed in the same way, shall be placed in another recess, with the teeth fitting into a denticle, which shall be fixed on the side of the second drum, and holes shall be made in that drum, as many as the number of miles of daily journey the chariot can make. Less or more is nothing to the purpose. And in all these holes shall be placed round stones, and in the case of that drum, or that recess, shall be made a single hole having a small channel, by which the stones which have been placed in that drum, when they come to that place, may fall individually into the box of the chariot and the brass vessel which shall be suppositum.

chunks.texto: Ita cum rota progrediens secum agat tympanum imum et denticulum eius singulis versationibus tympani superioris denticulos inpulsu cogat praeterire, efficiet, <ut,> cum CCCC imum versatum fuerit, superius tympanum semel circumagatur et denticulus, qui est ad latus eius fixus, unum denticulum tympani plani producat. Cum ergo CCCC versationibus imi tympani semel superius versabitur, progressus efficiet spatia pedum milia quinque, id est passus mille. Ex eo quot calculi deciderint sonando singula milia exisse monebunt. Numerus vero calculorum ex imo collectus summa diurni <itineris> miliariorum numerum indicabit.
chunks.traduccion: Thus, when the wheel advances, it drives the lower drum with it and its tooth with each rotation of the upper drum forces the teeth to pass by, so that when the lower drum has been rotated 400 times, the upper drum is rotated once and the tooth fixed to its side produces one tooth of the flat drum. Therefore, when the lower drum has been rotated once with 400 times, the progress will be 1,500 feet, that is, 1,000 paces. From this, the number of pebbles that have fallen will indicate by ringing that each thousand has passed. The number of pebbles collected from the bottom will indicate the total number of miles of the daily journey.

chunks.texto: Navigationibus vero similiter paucis rebus commutatis eadem ratione ⟨eadem⟩ efficiuntur. Namque traicitur per latera parietum axis habens extra navem prominentia capita, in quae includuntur rotae diametro pedum quaternûm, extantes habentes circa frontes adfixas pinnas aquam tangentes. Item medius axis in media navi ⟨habet⟩ tympanum cum uno denticulo extanti extra suam rotunditatem. Ad eum locum conlocatur loculamentum habens inclusum in se tympanum, peraequatis dentibus CCCC convenientibus denticulo tympani, quod est in axe inclusum, praeterea ad latus adfixum extantem extra rotunditatem alterum dentem unum.
chunks.traduccion: In the same way, with a few changes, navigation is achieved by the same method. For an axle is driven through the sides of the walls, having heads protruding beyond the ship, into which are enclosed wheels with a diameter of four and a half feet, having fins fixed around the fronts, touching the water. Likewise, the middle axle in the middle of the ship has a drum with one tooth protruding beyond its roundness. At that place is placed a pocket having a drum enclosed within it, with 400 equal teeth matching the tooth of the drum, which is enclosed in the axle, and on the other side is fixed another tooth protruding beyond its roundness.

chunks.texto: Insuper in altero loculamento cum eo confixo inclusum tympanum planum ad eundem modum dentatum, quibus dentibus <convenit> denticulus, qui est ad latus fixus tympano, quod est in cultro conlocatum ut eos dentes, qui sunt plani tympani, singulis versationibus singulos dens inpellendo in orbem planum tympanum verset. In plano autem tympano foramina fiant, in quibus foraminibus conlocabuntur calculi rotundi, In theca eius tympani, sive loculamentum est, unum foramen excavetur habens canaliculum, qua calculus liberatus ab obstantia cum ceciderit in vas aereum, sonitu significet.
chunks.traduccion: Moreover, in another cavity, fixed with it, is enclosed a flat tympanum, toothed in the same manner, with which teeth <fit> a small tooth, which is fixed to the side of the tympanum, which is placed in the knife so that those teeth, which are the flat tympanum, with each rotation, pushing each tooth into the plane of the tympanum turn it. Now in the flat tympanum are to be made holes, in which holes round stones will be placed. In the case of that tympanum, or cavity, one hole is to be dug out having a small canal, through which the stone, freed from obstacles, when it falls into the brass vessel, will produce a sound.

chunks.texto: Ita navis cum habuerit impetum aut remorum aut ventorum flatu, pinnae, quae erunt in rotis, tangentes aquam adversam vehementi retrorsus inpulsu coactae versabunt rotas; eae autem involvendo se agent axem, axis vero tympanum, cuius dens circumactus singulis versationibus singulos secundi tympani dentes inpellendo modicas efficiet circumitiones. Ita cum CCCC ab pinnis rotae fuerint versatae, semel tympanum circumactum inpellet dente, qui est ad latus fixus, plani tympani dentem. Igitur circumitio tympani plani quotienscumque ad foramen perducet calculos, emittet per canaliculum. Ita et sonitu et numero indicabit miliaria spatia navigationis.
chunks.traduccion: Thus when the ship has an impulse either by the oars or by the wind, the fins which will be on the wheels, touching the opposing water, will be forced by a strong backward thrust to turn the wheels; and these, by wrapping themselves, will drive the axle, and the axle the drum, whose tooth, turned round, with each rotation, drives each tooth of the second drum, making small revolutions. Thus when the wheels have been turned 400 times by the fins, once the drum has been turned round, it will drive the tooth, which is fixed to the side, of the flat drum. Therefore, whenever the revolution of the flat drum brings the pebbles to the hole, it will send them out through the canal. Thus it will indicate by both sound and number the miles of navigation.

chunks.texto: Nunc vero quae ad praesidia periculi et necessitatem salutis sunt inventa, id est scorpionum et ballistarum rationes, quibus symmetriis comparari possint, exponam.
chunks.traduccion: I shall now set forth what has been devised for defense in time of peril and for the preservation of safety — namely, the proportions of scorpions and ballistae, and the symmetries by which they may be constructed.

chunks.texto: Ipsûm tamen eorum foraminum capituli ⟨e magnitudine omnis⟩ deformatur altitudo et latitudo. Tabulae, quae sunt in summo et in imo capituli, peritretoe quae vocantur, fiant crassitudine unius foraminis, latitudine unius et eius dodrantis, in extremis foraminis unius et eius ⟨S⟩.
